units.source: A grisly aspect of Davkul, an ancient power not from this world, and the last remnants of {#1}brother name{/#1} from whose body it has been fashioned. It shall never break, but instead keep regrowing its scarred skin on the spot.
units.zh: 达夫库尔的骇人化身，凝聚着不属于这个世界的古老力量。它由{#1}那位弟兄{/#1}的肉身塑成，也是他最后的遗存。它永不破碎，伤痕累累的皮肤总会当即重新生长。

units.source: While along the roads, your wardogs suddenly scamper off and begin digging into the earth. You're not sure why as you don't recall giving either one a bone. A few moments later and they're fighting over what appears to be {#1}Finding{/#1}. You interrupt the tug of war, taking the goods for yourself. The hounds whine, but a few good pets settles them down.
units.zh: 行路途中，战犬们突然跑开，刨起地来。你不明所以，记得自己并没给过它们骨头。不一会儿，它们就为挖出的东西争抢起来，看上去是{#1}〈挖出的物品〉{/#1}。你打断这场拔河，把东西拿走。猎犬虽呜呜抱怨，摸了几下，便安静了。

units.source: {#1}Nonhedgeknight{/#1} sprints into your tent, nearly taking out one of the stakes and bringing the whole thing down. Sweat flies off his face and onto your maps. You look at the man with a stare that demands a good answer for what he's doing. He explains that the hedge knights {#2}Hedgeknight1{/#2} and {#3}Hedgeknight2{/#3} are getting into it. They've both picked up weapons and look about ready to kill each other. Having the two largest men in the company do battle probably isn't best for the health of... well, everyone. You quickly rush to the scene.
units.zh: {#1}另一名弟兄{/#1}冲进帐篷，差点撞掉帐桩，让整顶帐篷塌下来。汗水从他脸上甩到你的地图上。你盯着他，等一个足以解释这副样子的理由。他说，两个流浪骑士{#2}流浪骑士甲{/#2}与{#3}流浪骑士乙{/#3}闹起来了，双方都抄起了兵器，眼看要拼个你死我活。战团里最魁梧的两个人开打，对……嗯，对所有人的安危都不是好事。你连忙赶去现场。

units.source: {#1}Nonhedgeknight{/#1} calls out to you, asking you to stop the fight. The two hedge knights look over, each breath heaving their massive chests. You throw a dismissive hand. The knights nod and charge one another. The clash is loud, metal-shattering, bone-crunching. Growls follow every attempt to kill, so sonorous become the weapon swings. The sword catches the shaft of the giant axe and the two blades snap against one another. The hedge knights exchange cruel stares over the crossing, then quickly disarm and pull daggers, stabbing each other repeatedly as they fall to the ground. Neither man seems the least bit bothered by the wounds. They give up on the pitiful daggers and turn to using their own mitts, punching each other so fiercely you see teeth scattering amongst the bloodsprays.
units.zh: {#1}另一名弟兄{/#1}朝你喊话，求你阻止决斗。两名流浪骑士望过来，宽厚的胸膛随着呼吸剧烈起伏。你不以为意地挥挥手。骑士们点头，随即冲向彼此。撞击声震耳欲聋，混着金属崩裂与骨骼碎响。每一次杀招都伴着低吼，兵刃挥动也愈发沉重响亮。长剑架住巨斧的柄，两刃锵然相抵。两人隔着交错的武器狠盯对方，随即弃械拔匕首，一边跌向地面，一边接连刺向彼此。伤口似乎丝毫没让他们在意。他们又嫌小刀不过瘾，改用双拳，打得如此凶猛，你看见牙齿随着血沫四处飞溅。

units.source: You set yourself down on a stump and watch the rest of the fight. The men roll around on the ground, smashing each other in the face with punches that would kill a horse. Eventually, {#1}Hedgeknight1{/#1} squats on {#2}Hedgeknight2{/#2}'s shoulders. Seeing a rock nearby, {#3}Hedgeknight1{/#3} grabs it and cracks it over his opponent's skull. A bit of flesh is sheared off, revealing a slop of red and white beneath. The rock is brought down again. The brain pan splinters, shards of bone rupturing into fragments. {#4}Hedgeknight2{/#4} goes a bit limp, showing only a modicum of fight left in him. {#5}Hedgeknight1{/#5} punches his fist into the brainbox and rips out the namesake in one big gush of crimson. You gag at the sight, and a few men turn and vomit.
units.zh: 你在树桩上坐下，继续看这场决斗。两人在地上翻滚，用足以打死马的重拳猛砸对方的脸。最后，{#1}流浪骑士甲{/#1}骑上{#2}流浪骑士乙{/#2}的肩头。发现旁边有块石头，{#3}流浪骑士甲{/#3}抓起来，狠狠砸向对手头颅。皮肉被削掉一块，露出底下红白相间的烂糊。石头再次落下，颅骨裂开，骨片崩碎。{#4}流浪骑士乙{/#4}身子软了些，只剩一点挣扎的力气。{#5}流浪骑士甲{/#5}把拳头捣进破开的脑壳，猛地扯出大脑，鲜血顿时涌出。你看得直犯恶心，几个弟兄转身吐了。

units.source: You look to set yourself down on a nearby stump but jump back when the two hedge knights come barreling your way. {#1}Hedgeknight1{/#1}'s head smashes face first into what was to be your seat. He quickly turns around to face his assailant. All he meets is {#2}Hedgeknight2{/#2}'s boot, the interfacing of flesh and leather sounding off with a sickening clap. Now gargling on his own teeth, {#3}Hedgeknight1{/#3} asks if that's the best {#4}Hedgeknight2{/#4}'s got. To answer, {#5}Hedgeknight2{/#5} kicks him in the head again and again, and each rearing of his boot reveals {#6}Hedgeknight1{/#6} to be in a worse state, from bloodied red to a nightmarish twisting of flesh and eyelids and a flattened nose and a grin of horror where his teeth are either missing or hanging from blood engorged gums like they were nails on a skinless finger.
units.zh: 你正想坐到附近的树桩上，两名流浪骑士却猛冲过来，逼得你跳开。{#1}流浪骑士甲{/#1}的脸迎面撞在你原本要坐的位置。他赶紧翻身，面对袭击者，迎来的却只有{#2}流浪骑士乙{/#2}的靴子。皮肉与皮革相撞，发出令人作呕的脆响。{#3}流浪骑士甲{/#3}含着自己碎掉的牙齿，咕哝着问，{#4}流浪骑士乙{/#4}就这点本事吗？作为回答，{#5}流浪骑士乙{/#5}一次次踢向他的脑袋。靴子每抬起一回，{#6}流浪骑士甲{/#6}的模样便更惨几分：先是满脸鲜红，继而皮肉与眼皮扭曲得如同噩梦，鼻子塌陷，咧开的嘴骇人至极。牙齿不是缺失，就是挂在充血的牙龈上，像无皮手指上的指甲。

units.source: Finally, the brainpan is crushed, the series of splintering boneplates sounding like something falling through a winter tree's branches. You turn your gaze in abhorrence, but some brothers cannot, one spews vomit. Peeking to see what damage was done, you see {#1}Hedgeknight2{/#1}'s heel is halfway down a throat and the toe of his boot is churning another man's brain. He curses as he struggles to retrieve what delivered the killing blow.
units.zh: 终于，颅骨被踩碎了，骨板接连迸裂的声音，像有什么从冬日的树枝间一路坠下。你厌恶地移开目光，有些弟兄却挪不开眼，其中一人吐了出来。你又瞥了一眼，只见{#1}流浪骑士乙{/#1}的脚跟已陷入对方喉中，靴尖正在搅动脑浆。他一边咒骂，一边试着拔出那只完成致命一击的脚。

units.source: "What say you, travelers, care for a show? A mere {#1}{#2}Payment{/#2}{/#1} crowns to entertain you all evening!"
units.zh: "旅人们，怎么样，要不要看场戏？只需{#1}{#2}〈费用〉{/#2}{/#1}克朗，就能让各位痛快一整晚！"

units.source: {#1}Entertainer{/#1} steps forward and picks up some of the troupe's tools of trade. He tests them out, impressing the entertainers with how well he's able to use their own equipment. The mime asks if perhaps they could play a couple of tunes with him. He nods and joins the entertainers, putting on a show that's for the ages. When it's all over, the troupe is so impressed that they try and recruit the man. You tell them that ain't happening and {#2}Entertainer{/#2} nods.
units.zh: {#1}会表演的弟兄{/#1}走上前，拿起剧团的几件家伙什试了试。借来的道具在他手里竟使得如此娴熟，艺人们都看呆了。哑剧演员问，能否与他合演几曲？他点头加入，众人献上一场足以长久流传的好戏。演完后，剧团佩服得想把他招走。你告诉他们，这不可能，{#2}会表演的弟兄{/#2}也点了点头。

units.source: You order the troupe raided. The mime, this time actually in character, holds up his hands and mouths 'what?'. But the playfulness is wiped away when {#1}Randombrother{/#1} walks up and plants a punch right on his chin. The mime goes down with a catlike cry, mewling in the mud as he nurses his jaw.
units.zh: 你下令抢劫剧团。这一回，哑剧演员倒还记得自己的身份，举起双手，无声地做出“什么？”的口型。可{#1}某位弟兄{/#1}上前一拳砸在他下巴上，顷刻间打散了那点诙谐。他像猫一样尖叫着倒下，捂着下巴，在泥地里哀鸣。

units.source: The rest of the company knocks the troupe around while raiding their wagon for goods. A juggler gets kicked right in the balls and a singer has her throat chopped by {#1}Randombrother2{/#1}'s hand. The sword swallower tries to hide his sword the only place he knows where, but a mercenary retrieves it with a rather painful unsheathing. The firebreather drinks the entirety of his jug then asks if you want to take that, too. You have him gut-punched for his snark.
units.zh: 其余弟兄一边殴打剧团成员，一边翻上货车搜刮。耍杂技的被一脚踢中卵蛋，女歌手则挨了{#1}另一位弟兄{/#1}一记手刀，正中喉咙。吞剑人想把剑藏进自己最熟悉的地方，可一名佣兵又用极其痛苦的方式把它“拔”了出来。喷火艺人喝光整壶东西，问你是不是连这也想拿走。你让人往他肚子上揍了一拳，好教他别耍嘴皮子。

units.source: "Ah, interested in a map are ya? This here cartographical, topographical, geographical oddity carried by a man who, I assure you, is quite sensical! This here paper tells you the exact location of the famous '{#1}Location{/#1}'. I'm sure you've heard about it, yes? Host to untold treasures! Resting place of some this world's finest arms! And all it'll cost you is a meager {#2}{#3}Cost{/#3}{/#2} crowns!"
units.zh: "啊，对地图有兴趣？这可是制图学、地形学、地理学的奇珍，拿着它的人却绝不古怪，这点我向你保证！这张纸能告诉你，鼎鼎大名的“{#1}〈地点名〉{/#1}”究竟在哪。你一定听说过吧？那里藏着数不尽的财宝！还埋藏着世间最精良的兵器！而你只需花区区{#2}{#3}〈价格〉{/#3}{/#2}克朗！"

units.source: "So we've decided to not purchase it at your original asking price. That much is clear. So, friend, I think we will purchase it for {#1}{#2}Cost{/#2}{/#1}. That is fair to all parties involved, and surely a fine businessman such as yourself can see a deal! We're hardly businessmen ourselves, but we know that's a good deal!"
units.zh: "所以，我们已经决定，不按你原先的开价买。这一点很清楚。那么，朋友，我看我们出{#1}{#2}〈价格〉{/#2}{/#1}买下它吧。这个价钱对双方都公平，像你这么精明的生意人，肯定看得出这是笔好买卖！我们算不上什么生意人，可连我们都知道这买卖划算！"

units.source: While you're talking to the merchant, {#1}Thief{/#1} the thief sidles up next to you, appearing rather interested in the conversation. He glances at you. You do a double take. He grins and nods. You quickly eye the salesman then glance back at the thief and nod. The merchant is in the middle of his sales pitch and sees none of this. He keeps talking, but you hear little of it. You just know to keep nodding for a merchant such as he only tells you things you want to hear anyway.
units.zh: 你正与商人交谈，{#1}盗贼{/#1}悄悄凑到身边，对话题似乎颇感兴趣。他瞥你一眼，你又看了他一眼。他咧嘴笑着点头，你迅速扫过商人，再回望小偷，也点了点头。商人正忙着推销，丝毫没察觉。他继续滔滔不绝，你却没听进多少，只知道跟着点头就行——这类商人，说的反正都是你爱听的话。

units.source: The sellsword picks up the 'pitch bucket' and hurls it completely over the fruit fornicator. The man screams as the hot liquids sizzle and a rather potent order wisps into a smoky air. You watch as {#1}Otherbro{/#1} grabs a few naked chickens - not their feathers, just the chickens themselves - and starts beating the melon mugger with them like an angry frock swinging chained censers. The tarred man hollers out, partly in pain, partly confused. The crowd, also confused, reluctantly cheers. When he's finished, {#2}Otherbro{/#2} drops the chickens, which are but a slop of drooping meat and tar at this point. He wipes his forehead.
units.zh: 佣兵提起“沥青桶”，将桶里的东西全泼在那个糟蹋水果的家伙身上。热液滋滋作响，那人惨叫起来，浓烈气味飘入烟雾。接着，{#1}另一位弟兄{/#1}抓起几只拔光毛的鸡——不是羽毛，就是鸡本身——抡起来痛打瓜男，活像暴怒的教士挥着链香炉。浑身焦油的男人嚎个不停，一半因为疼，一半因为搞不懂这是什么刑罚。围观者同样困惑，却仍勉强喝起彩。打完，{#2}另一位弟兄{/#2}丢下鸡，那些鸡此时已成了软垂的肉与焦油混成的一团。他抹了抹额头。

units.source: On his command, the mob of children start hurling stones from the treeline. The sellswords band together, holding shields up in a formation akin to a tortoise, and slowly move forward. It's a strange effort, like a shell-game artist sliding his cup over the ball, but the company manages to grab the merchant's goods and slide away out of the field, all the while being pelted from every which way. The little leader kid shakes his fist at you. You give him the finger and start back onto the path where you take a good look at the merchant's goods. {#1}Randombrother{/#1} stares at the rewards while rubbing a welt on his forehead.
units.zh: 他一声令下，孩子们纷纷从林缘投出石头。佣兵聚拢起来，举盾结成龟壳般的阵形，缓缓向前挪动。这场面着实古怪，活像街头耍把戏的人把杯子滑到小球上方。不过，战团总算搬走了商人的货物，又顶着四面八方飞来的石头，一点点退离了空地。领头的小鬼朝你挥舞拳头，你回敬他一根中指，走回道路，仔细查看缴获的货物。{#1}某位弟兄{/#1}盯着战利品，揉着额头上的肿包。

units.source: When the mercenary reaches in, the wildman swipes out. It's too fast to even see. {#1}Taskedbro{/#1} slowly turns around. There's a black hole where one of his eyes used to be. The wildman squishes the eye between his teeth, a white goop bursting forth like a popped pustule, and it turns into a filmy paste as he chews. The animal tamer throws you a sack of crowns and runs off.
units.zh: 佣兵刚把手伸进去，荒野人便猛地挥爪，快得根本看不清。{#1}负责清理的弟兄{/#1}缓缓转过身，原本一只眼睛的位置已经变成了黑洞。荒野人用牙齿挤破那颗眼球，白色浆液像脓疮破裂般迸出，随着咀嚼化成一团黏糊糊的东西。驯兽师丢给你一袋克朗，转身就跑。

units.source: If anyone in the party could help talk the caged wildman down, it's probably {#1}Wildman{/#1}. He goes to the cage, stares in. There's an exchange of hoots. Your wildman raps the bars with a knuckle, and the prisoner raps back and hoots somberly. Suddenly, {#2}Wildman{/#2} grabs the animal tamer by the head and drives him into the bars. You go to save the tamer, but the imprisoned wildman soars across the cage with atavistic terror in his eyes. Stepping back for your own safety, you can only watch as this bestial man sets upon the tamer. Both wildmen pull and drag on the man's face. The concussed man groggily yells.
units.zh: 队伍里若有人能劝笼中的荒野人冷静下来，那多半就是{#1}团里的荒野人{/#1}。他走到笼边，往里盯着，两人互相吼了几声。你的荒野人用指节敲敲铁栏，囚犯也敲了回去，发出低沉的哀鸣。突然，{#2}团里的荒野人{/#2}抓住驯兽师的脑袋，猛地撞上栏杆。你本想去救人，笼中的荒野人却已冲过来，眼中迸发着原始而骇人的凶光。为保自身安全，你只得后退，眼看着这个兽性十足的人扑向驯兽师。两个荒野人一同撕扯他的脸。被撞得神志不清的驯兽师含糊大喊。

units.source: {#1}Wildman{/#1} corks his thumbs into the man's eyes while the imprisoned wildman grips the tamer's mouth and pulls down. His head is literally ripped apart by the seams and sinews. A few men vomit as the tamer's brains falls out where his tongue should be, a truly awful way of speaking one's mind. The 'warden' taken care of, {#2}Wildman{/#2} looks at you and at the wildman with a sort of 'can we keep him?' gesture.
units.zh: {#1}团里的荒野人{/#1}将拇指深深按进他的眼睛，笼中的荒野人则攥住他的嘴，往下猛扯。脑袋沿着骨缝和筋腱被生生撕开，脑浆从本该是舌头的地方淌出，恶心得几个弟兄当场吐了出来。这回他真把脑子里的东西全“说”了出来，场面惨不忍睹。解决了“狱卒”之后，{#2}团里的荒野人{/#2}看看你，又看看笼中的荒野人，比划出一副“我们能留下他吗”的意思。

His face is ripped apart like a loaf of old bread, a couple of coathangers for a jawbone, a tongue lolling like an uprooted snake. {#1}Monk{/#1} vomits as his face is doused in blood. {#2}Otherbrother{/#2} shakes his head.

units.source: It'd be a crime to leave these animals out here to starve and rot. And it'd also be a terrible waste of good meat. You have the creatures slaughtered. It's an easy, albeit brutal job, stabbing and slicing a bunch of hapless critters and beasts. The bear is the last to go, and it does not go easily. It manages to drag {#1}Hurtbro{/#1} close for a nasty swipe, but beyond that your men put it to a slow, grisly death. The rest of the wagons are turned over and looted.
units.zh: 把这些动物丢在这里活活饿死、腐烂，未免造孽，何况还糟蹋了这么多好肉。你叫人将它们宰了。这活轻松，却很残忍，无非是对着一群无助的大小禽兽捅刺劈砍。熊留到最后，也最不肯就范：它将{#1}一名弟兄{/#1}拖近，狠狠拍了一爪。不过除此之外，弟兄们终究让它缓慢而惨烈地死去。其余货车也被翻查、搜刮一空。

units.source: {#1}Archer{/#1} nocks an arrow and sticks his tongue out as he aims up the tree. The girl and boy don't seem fond of this idea and clap their hands over their eyes. The archer looses the shot and it cracks against the cat's branch, breaking it and sending the cat cartwheeling down the tree like a game of devil sticks. When it hits the ground, the boy and girl lunge on it. They pet it and thank you for your troubles. The girl squeezes the cat warmly.
units.zh: {#1}弓手{/#1}搭上箭，吐着舌头，抬头瞄向树梢。两个孩子似乎不怎么赞成这个主意，连忙用手捂住眼睛。弓手一箭射出，正中猫栖着的树枝。枝条应声折断，猫像杂耍用的花棍一样，翻着跟头一路滚下树来。刚一落地，男孩和女孩就扑了过去。他们摸着猫，感谢你费心相助。女孩亲热地抱紧它。

units.source: {#1}Archer{/#1} readies himself, nocking an arrow and taking aim. The cat purrs as it stares down the line of the shot, rather sublime in its suicidal stance. Closing one eye, the archer lets the arrow fly. There isn't much mewling to be had. The cat tumbles down the tree like a game of devil sticks and lands on the ground with an arrow shaft halfway out its head. The girl crouches down and stares at the slinky bit of brain wobbling off the arrowtip. She looks up at you, as though it were you who fired the shot.

Even some of the men are impressed by the fella's feline-like reflexes!

units.source: {#1}Witchhunter{/#1} steps forward with a skeptical eye. He looks at the woman who strains to say 'please.' The witch hunter stares her up and down, then he turns and drives a blade through the man holding the torch. He gargles with it in his throat and his hands work to try and pry it out.

units.source: And with that, {#1}Witchhunter{/#1} drives his weapon into the evil spirit's skull. The skin hardens like a desert earth before chipping away.

units.source: The monk, {#1}Monk{/#1}, sits with the town's own friar and talks for a time. When they are done, a nod is given to the torchman who sets the wooden pallets aflame. The woman screams for mercy, but the flames have none for her, slowly working up feet first. It is a horrific sight and only when the smoke is a choking cloud does the dying woman go silent. The fire consumes her entirely as the rest of the town claps and cheers. {#2}Monk{/#2} states that she was clearly a witch and had to be done away with. You're not sure. All you saw was a woman burned alive, but you trust that he knows more than you about the war between the old gods and the evils of sorcery.
units.zh: {#1}修士{/#1}与镇上的修士坐下来谈了一阵。谈完后，其中一人向执火把的人点头，后者便点燃了木架。女人尖叫着求饶，火焰却毫不留情，从她双脚开始慢慢向上爬。场面惨不忍睹，直到浓烟汇成令人窒息的云团，垂死的女人才终于没了声音。烈火将她完全吞没，镇民们却拍手欢呼。{#2}修士{/#2}说，她显然是个女巫，必须铲除。你并不确定。你看见的只是一个女人被活活烧死，但对于旧神与邪恶巫术之间的斗争，你相信他懂得比你多。

units.source: {#1}Randombrother{/#1} gives the thief a proper beating with a short cane. The shaft lands viciously hard and you can hear the sound of the blows passing through the man's almost hollow frame. He wilts and turns and tries hard to get away, but the sellsword is persistent in meting out the punishment. When it's all said and done, you leave the beaten man behind, wimpering and clutching the dirt between his frail fingers.
units.zh: {#1}某位弟兄{/#1}拿短棍狠狠教训了盗贼一顿。每一下都打得凶，声音穿过那副几乎空空的骨架。他蜷缩、扭动，拼命想躲，可佣兵始终不肯停手。惩罚结束，你们把挨打的人留在原地，任他呜咽着，用纤弱的手指抓紧泥土。

units.source: While approaching {#1}Townname{/#1}, a local man waves you down. He's standing beside the skeleton of what appears to be a mill. Exasperated, he explains that his laborers didn't show up today and he needs to finish the mill before a local baron arrives. If he doesn't finish it, the baron might not ever give him another contract. You do have a few former laborers in the company. Perhaps they can be used to help the man?
units.zh: 接近{#1}〈城镇名〉{/#1}时，一个当地人挥手拦下你。他站在一座像是磨坊的建筑框架旁，焦急地解释，工人今天没来，可他必须赶在当地男爵到访前完工。不然，男爵可能再也不会给他工程做。战团里倒有几个当过工人的弟兄，或许能派去帮忙？

units.source: You agree to lend a few of the {#1}Companyname{/#1}'s finest to the project. When it's all said and done, the local man comes to you grinning ear-to-ear. He hands a satchel over.

units.source: {#1}Swordmaster{/#1} enters your tent. You wave him to the chair across your table. He sits so slowly and feebly that you fear him standing back up will take twice as long. units.source: "Where you're from is a house, not a home. You yearn for a different place in a different time, when you're in this place, right here, right now. The {#1}Companyname{/#1} looks after you, and you it, and only together will we persevere."

units.source: "Hey, thinking of the old is good for the soul, even if it's through a thicket of shit and cruelty and evil and all else that makes any man stay up at night. But it's only good for a time. You look at the past, you acknowledge it, and then you move on. You have to be sure to only visit the past, not dwell in it. Everyone here has a past, {#1}Disowned{/#1}, and in that respect you will never be alone."
units.zh: "嘿，回想往事对人有好处，哪怕那些往事满是烂事、残忍、邪恶，以及种种让人彻夜难眠的东西。可回想也得有个限度。看看过去，认清它，然后继续往前走。记住，你只能回去看看，不能住在那里。这里每个人都有自己的过去，{#1}被逐贵族{/#1}，在这件事上，你永远不会孤单。"

units.source: "Yeah, yeah, that's right. I guess a part of me was worried that I was genuinely wanting to return there. I was picturing it with the hearth alight, smoke out of the chimney, soft candlelight beyond the windows, and my family there awaiting me. I was ignoring the locked door, the guard dogs squatting outside, and those I love telling me to never come back lest it's in a box to bury far beneath the earth. I wasn't thinking of my past so much as dreaming of it, and I think you've helped me realize that, captain. Thank you. I know that, one day, I shan't have to dream about the {#1}Companyname{/#1}, but instead remember it clearly and fondly."
units.zh: "是啊，是啊，你说得对。我想，我心里一直有点担心，怕自己其实还想回去。我想象炉火正旺，烟囱里冒着烟，窗后透出柔和的烛光，家人正等着我。可我忘了紧锁的大门，忘了守在外面的恶犬，也忘了那些我爱的人曾说，永远别再回来，除非装在棺材里，好让他们把我埋到地底深处。我不是在回忆过去，而是在梦里美化它。团长，是你让我明白了这一点，谢谢。我知道，终有一天，想起{#1}〈战团名〉{/#1}时，我不必靠做梦；我会清楚地记得这里，心怀眷恋。"

units.source: While walking the streets of {#1}Townname{/#1}, you come upon a crowd standing around a hanged man. He must have been of some notoriety: the folks are muscling one another to try and get a turn to cut a toe or finger off as a sort of hanging-heirloom. An old man is quickly elbowed out of the mob. He turns to you, voice raspy, his bony fingers tented like sickly ribs.

You retrieve your sellsword and leave before the old man lops your head with the most longwinded and one-sided conversation ever.
units.zh: 他唠叨不休，你四下寻找{#1}一名弟兄{/#1}，却见他刚从女人家里出来，那位女士脸上还带着一抹……再明显不过的红晕。你领回自己的佣兵，赶在老人用史上最漫长的单方面谈话把你脑袋念掉之前，离开了。

units.source: The old man was doing repairs atop the wooden wellhead when it broke apart. Unfortunately, if you're standing atop a wellhead when it goes bust there's only one place to go: down. Very, very far down. As you look over the edge of the well, you can see the old man floating in a matter that is most unlively. {#1}Otherbrother{/#1} sidles up next to you and whispers, using a hand to keep his words from being heard.
units.zh: 老人站在井口的木架上修东西，木架却突然散了。可惜，人站在井架上时，脚下要是塌了，就只剩一个去处：往下掉。而且要掉很深，很深。你探头往井里看，见老人浮在水面上，那姿态怎么看都不像还活着。{#1}一名弟兄{/#1}悄悄挪到你身边，用手掩着嘴，低声说道。

units.source: You walk to the base of the enormity and run a hand along its bark, but then you stop, fearing that your flesh may have just trespassed upon holy ground like a child tumbling playfully into a church of one wholly quiet crowd. {#1}Monk{/#1} the monk comes to your side nodding and with his hands firmly behind his back.

units.source: A rugged dog such as he would make for a great mascot. The little mutt could definitely boost morale. You order {#1}Bro{/#1} to feed it some food in the hopes that it'll tag along. He goes out with a scrap of leftovers and crouches down.
units.zh: 这么一条皮实的狗，正适合当战团的吉祥物。小家伙肯定能让弟兄们高兴些。你叫{#1}一名弟兄{/#1}拿点吃的喂它，希望它肯留下。他拿着一块剩饭剩肉走过去，蹲下身。

units.source: You ask {#1}Houndmaster{/#1} the houndmaster if he can try and 'woo' this dog. He nods and steps toward it. The wild mongrel's ears go from pinned to pointed. Crouched, the houndmaster slowly edges his way toward the beast. He keeps his hand out with a piece of meat in the palm. Hunger overcomes heedfulness and the dog sniffs its way ever closer to the houndmaster's hand. The dog tongues it out of his palm and chows down. The dog trainer feeds him another bite. He scruffs him up and finds the sweet spot behind his ears. Looking back, {#2}Houndmaster{/#2} nods.
units.zh: 你问{#1}驯犬师{/#1}，能不能试着把这条狗“哄”过来。他点点头，迈步上前。那杂毛野狗原本紧贴脑后的耳朵顿时竖了起来。驯犬师蹲下身，一点点挪近，伸出的手掌里放着一块肉。饥饿终究压过了戒心，狗一边嗅，一边靠近他的手，伸舌卷走肉块，狼吞虎咽地吃了。驯犬师又喂了一口，揉揉它的皮毛，找准耳根后最舒服的地方挠起来。{#2}驯犬师{/#2}回过头，点了点头。

units.zh: 你与弟兄们围坐火旁，火堆对面的争论渐渐高了起来。{#1}拳斗者{/#1}站起身，指着自己的胸口哈哈大笑。

units.source: The slightest suggestion that {#1}Brawler{/#1}'s fists weren't made of jaw-demolishing bricks kicks off a brutal fight. The brawlers grab one another and swing their free hands in looping undercuts. Each punch lands with cracking ferocity. Surely no man could take so much damage and stay on his feet, but here you're witnessing two fellas doing just that. You order the company to break up the fight.
units.zh: 仅仅暗示{#1}拳斗者{/#1}的拳头不是专砸下巴的砖头，就足以引发一场恶斗。两人互相揪住对方，腾出另一只手，接连抡起下勾拳。每一拳都砸得令人心惊。常人挨上这么多下，早该倒了，可你眼前这两个偏偏还站着。你命令弟兄们上前拉架。

units.zh: {#1}拳斗者{/#1}捏住一侧鼻孔，从另一侧喷出一股血，耸了耸肩。

units.source: It is here you find {#1}Monk{/#1} and {#2}Flagellant{/#2} talking to one another. Their discussion is, at first, an easy one. The monk pleads with the flagellant to set aside his whip. While you don't necessarily wish to step in, you can't help but agree that destroying your own body on a glorified gore-schedule is not the best way to live. But then the flagellant retorts with something that gives you both pause. It is a phrase so well crafted that to think it might justify the man's personal habits has you pushing the notion out of your head as fast as possible. Disturbing, too, was the ease with which he said it. That such a soothing voice could be so warmly bundled in that scarred husk of flesh. What could muster it?
units.zh: 你在这里看见{#1}修士{/#1}与{#2}苦修者{/#2}正在交谈。起初，这场谈话并不难懂：修士恳求苦修者放下鞭子。你虽不一定想插手，却也不得不同意，按着一套被奉为神圣的流血日程摧残自己，实在算不上好活法。可苦修者随后的反驳，让你们都愣住了。那句话说得如此巧妙，竟似乎真能替他的所作所为辩护，你只得赶紧将这个念头赶出脑海。更令人不安的是，他说得那么从容：如此舒缓的嗓音，竟能温暖地藏在那具伤痕累累的皮囊里。究竟是什么支撑着它？

units.source: {#1}Gambler{/#1}, the man with a gambling problem, has apparently gone around camp asking men to play a game of horseshoes - with a few crowns on the line, of course. It appears that {#2}Minstrel{/#2}, the wily minstrel, has obliged him and taken the bet. He says he's pretty good at the game to which the gambler responds that he is the best.
units.zh: {#1}赌徒{/#1}显然在营里问了一圈，想找人玩掷马蹄铁——当然，得押上几个克朗。机灵的{#2}吟游诗人{/#2}似乎答应奉陪，接下了赌局。他说自己挺擅长，赌徒则表示，自己可是个中第一。

units.source: The two men heave horseshoes until their arms tire and the sun wanes. Nobody is the winner as the game can't move off of a tie. After another indecisive round, {#1}Minstrel{/#1} says he'll go for a double-or-nothing round if they go left-handed. {#2}Gambler{/#2} agrees. He goes first, throwing three horseshoes. The first two go haywire, but the third manages to spin around the ring. He grins as he wishes the minstrel good luck. {#3}Minstrel{/#3} nods and rolls up his sleeves. He sticks his tongue out and slims his eyes, lining up the shot. His feet do a little tap-dance and just before he throws he looks back and says,
units.zh: 两人一直掷到胳膊发酸，夕阳西沉。谁也没赢，比分始终打平。又一轮不分胜负后，{#1}吟游诗人{/#1}提议，换左手再来一轮，赢了双倍，输了清零。{#2}赌徒{/#2}答应了。他先掷，连扔三枚马蹄铁。前两枚都飞偏了，第三枚总算绕着桩子落稳。他咧嘴一笑，祝吟游诗人好运。{#3}吟游诗人{/#3}点头，挽起袖子，吐出舌尖，眯眼瞄准，脚下还轻轻踢踏了几步。出手前，他忽然回过头说。

units.source: Something of a commotion draws you from your tent. Men are sitting on a few stumps or on the ground, eagerly watching something in the distance. With squinting eyes, you spot {#1}Clown{/#1} and {#2}Archer{/#2} doing something odd. An apple rests on one man's head, while the other is walking away - a bow in hand.

units.source: {#1}Archer{/#1} angles his shoulders to {#2}Clown{/#2} and draws his bow, the silhouette of the man but a crescent of wood, string, and arm. You can't see {#3}Clown{/#3}'s face, but you assume his eyes are closed. The shot is released. It zips. It disappears. {#4}Clown{/#4} rocks backward, clutching his face. This isn't looking good. The man screams. The crowd oohs. {#5}Archer{/#5} slowly lowers his bow and looks at it as though it is at fault.
units.zh: {#1}弓手{/#1}侧身对准{#2}耍宝的弟兄{/#2}，拉开长弓。人影、弓身、弓弦和手臂，绷成一弯紧紧的月牙。你看不清{#3}耍宝的弟兄{/#3}的脸，不过猜他大概闭着眼。箭出弦了，嗖的一声，转眼便没了踪影。{#4}耍宝的弟兄{/#4}猛地向后一仰，双手捂住脸。看来不妙。那人惨叫起来，围观者齐齐倒吸一口凉气。{#5}弓手{/#5}慢慢放下弓，盯着它看，仿佛错全在弓上。

units.source: The men cheer as you give an affirming nod. You take a seat amongst them as {#1}Archer{/#1} and {#2}Clown{/#2} get ready, the former nocking an arrow while the latter balances an apple atop his head. When the fruit is good and steady, the archer draws back his bow, forming but a silhouette of man, wood, and string, a crescent of determination as he aims downfield. The men are exchanging bets on whether or not he misses. You want to look away, but the spectacle truly is too much.
units.zh: 你点头应允，弟兄们立刻欢呼起来。你在众人中间坐下，{#1}弓手{/#1}与{#2}耍宝的弟兄{/#2}开始准备：前者搭好箭，后者小心地将苹果顶稳。等果子不再晃动，弓手拉满弓弦，人影、木弓与细弦绷成一弯月牙，稳稳地瞄向场地另一头。弟兄们纷纷下注，赌他会不会射偏。你想别过头去，可这场面实在让人移不开眼。

units.source: A great gasp follows the arrow's release, as though some ominous event long foretold had finally happened. Men reel back in their seats, wincing and gritting their teeth. The apple is shot off {#1}Clown{/#1}'s head, fruit and arrow spinning away. After a brief silence, the men erupt in cheers. {#2}Clown{/#2} takes a bow, while {#3}Archer{/#3} slackens his draw and looks a bit relieved.
units.zh: 箭一离弦，众人便齐齐惊呼，仿佛预言已久的凶兆终于应验。有人向后缩，有人龇牙咧嘴，紧紧咬住牙关。苹果从{#1}耍宝的弟兄{/#1}头顶飞了出去，连同箭矢一起翻滚。短暂的寂静过后，欢呼声骤然爆发。{#2}耍宝的弟兄{/#2}躬身谢幕，{#3}弓手{/#3}则松下弓，明显舒了口气。

units.source: You hear a yelp and quickly rush to the noise. When you get there, you're not sure whether it was man or dog that produced it. {#1}Butcher{/#1} the butcher is holding a cleaver up and a wardog is rearing beneath him, both sides ready to lunge. The man sees you and quickly sweeps the weapon behind his back. The hound takes a squat and throws some puppy eyes your way. Raising an eyebrow, you try not to make sense of the scene.
units.zh: 你听见一声尖叫，赶忙循声跑去。到了近前，却分不清刚才叫的是人还是狗。{#1}屠夫{/#1}举着剁肉刀，一条战犬在他面前龇牙，两边都摆着随时扑上去的架势。那人看见你，立刻把刀藏到背后；狗也蹲下来，冲你露出可怜巴巴的眼神。你挑挑眉，懒得深究眼前这一幕。

units.source: You step out of your tent to survey the men. A great many of them are freshly hired grunts, nervously buddying up with one another or trying their hand at some of the weapons. {#1}Oldguard{/#1} comes to your side.
units.zh: 你走出帐篷，巡视弟兄们。许多人刚刚入伙，有的紧张地找人结伴，有的正笨拙地试用武器。{#1}老兵{/#1}来到你身边。

units.source: {#1}Oldguard{/#1} tells the recruits to take up weapons. When every single one of them picks up a sword, the old guard yells at them, stating that not every foe hankering for you being graveyard dead is gonna be wielding the exact same blade. A few nod before hurriedly exchanging their swords for axes and spears. With the crew equipped, the training begins. Mostly, {#2}Oldguard{/#2} teaches basics like how a formation makes it easier to defend not only one another, but also yourself.
units.zh: {#1}老兵{/#1}让新兵拿起武器。结果人人都挑了剑，老兵当即开骂：想把你们送进坟地的敌人，可不会全拿一模一样的兵器。几个人连忙点头，换上斧头和长矛。众人装备妥当，训练开始。{#2}老兵{/#2}主要教些基本功，比如怎样结阵，既护住同伴，也更容易保全自己。

units.source: The men take practiced shots downrange, the arrows peppering all around their targets, a scant few lucky ones going where they should. {#1}Oldguard{/#1} spends the rest of the day exhaustingly having the men shoot and shoot and shoot until luck is squeezed out of the equation altogether.

units.source: The apprentice {#1}Apprentice{/#1} has apparently become a ward to {#2}Teacher{/#2}. While the swordmaster is long in the tooth, he seems quite eager to help the young man become a better fighter. The apprentice uses a real sword, the swordmaster but a wooden one. It is in this rather large difference of chosen weaponry that the swordmaster displays the usefulness of positioning, finding openings, and getting out of the way of danger.

Unfortunately, they are using the company dining equipment to set up little dolls to beat up. The young lad has certainly made a mess of those pots and pans in his continuous pursuit of being a better fighter.

units.source: It appears as though {#1}Teacher{/#1} the ol' sellsword has a little bird following him around: young {#2}Apprentice{/#2}. Now in the company of mercenaries, the apprentice must want to learn from those with plenty of experience on the road earning blood money. While they train, you notice that the sellsword puts most of his emphasis on exercising one's body. Being faster than your opponent and outlasting him are just as important as putting a blade through his brainbox. The earnest lad seems increasingly sturdy, earning some sense of vigor you did not notice before.
units.zh: {#1}老佣兵{/#1}身后似乎多了只跟脚的小鸟：年轻的{#2}学徒{/#2}。如今既然进了佣兵团，学徒自然想向那些常年在刀口上挣钱的人讨教。看他们训练时，你发现老佣兵尤其看重身体的锻炼：比对手更快、比对手更能撑，与一剑扎进对方脑壳同样重要。小伙子练得认真，身板也越来越结实，渐渐显出从前不曾有过的精神劲儿。

units.source: A couple of times now you've caught {#1}Apprentice{/#1} watching {#2}Teacher{/#2} from a distance. The young apprentice seems rather enraptured by the hedge knight's brute violence. After a few days, the knight relents, asking the lad to come and have a chat. You know not what they say, but now you've noticed they have been training together. The hedge knight is not a kind trainer, either. He beats the boy frequently, toughening him up. At first, the apprentice flinches before every strike, but now you see that he is showing a little more resolve in the face of such towering adversity. The hedge knight is also showing the man how to kill fast and efficiently. Little mind is paid to defense in these talks you overhear, but who needs to defend themselves from a dead opponent?
units.zh: 你已经好几次撞见{#1}学徒{/#1}远远地盯着{#2}流浪骑士{/#2}看。年轻学徒似乎被那位流浪骑士凶猛粗暴的打法迷住了。过了几天，骑士终于松口，叫小伙子过去聊聊。你不知道他们说了什么，只发现此后两人开始一起训练。流浪骑士可不是个温柔的老师，动不动就揍徒弟，非要把他练结实不可。起初，学徒每次挨打前都会畏缩，如今面对这座山一般的对手，倒渐渐稳住了心神。骑士也教他如何干净利落地杀人。你偶尔听见他们讲解招式，几乎不提防守——可对手既然已经死了，又有什么可防的？

units.source: The men of the {#1}Companyname{/#1} stagger and fall and don't get back up with quite the speed they used to. A few have taken to coughing fits and others look about ready to succumb to exhaustion. Only the strongest of the bunch carry on with no problem. It is those men who surely share a link with the ancestors of this horrid land.
units.zh: {#1}〈战团名〉{/#1}的弟兄们踉跄跌倒，爬起来的速度已远不如从前。有人咳嗽不止，有人眼看就要被疲惫压垮。只有其中最强壮的几人仍能照常赶路。想必这些人，与这片可怕土地上的先民流着相似的血。

units.source: "So, what say we help take the edge off, hm? Been a long day, no? For that many men, I'd wager it'd cost you a low {#1}{#2}Cost{/#2}{/#1} crowns."

units.source: {#1}Bowyer{/#1} the bowyer comes to you with a bit of request: he wishes to build a weapon for the ages. Apparently, the man has been attempting to build a bow of legendary qualities for many years, but now that he has been on the road he's picked up a few things to fill in his gaps of knowledge. Truly, he believes he can get it right this time. All he needs is a few resources to help procure the elements needed to construct it. A sum of 500 crowns is what he humbly requests, and the quality wood you carry.
units.zh: {#1}制弓匠{/#1}来找你，提出一个请求：他想造一件足以传世的兵器。多年来，他一直想做出一张传奇般的好弓，却始终未能如愿。如今四处闯荡，他又学到了不少东西，补上了过去欠缺的门道。他相信，这次一定能成。眼下只差些物资，好备齐制弓所需的材料。他谦恭地请求你拨出500克朗，再加上战团带着的那些优质木材。

Surely no man will be accidentally wielding that thing!

provenance.game_source: %randombrother% draws his weapon and the man backs off. The horse owner spits and shakes his head.

units.source: The flagellant drop the whip's strings, twirls them around for a moment, then strikes. The hanging man cries out. A wound opens and gapes from the tip of one rib clear across his back to the tip of another. You can see the muscle and fat bubbling beneath. {#1}Flagellant{/#1} strikes again, and again, and again. Blood splashes the flagellant as he works and the horse-porker has long since passed out. Eventually, one of the men gets to his feet and takes the whip back.
units.zh: 苦修者垂下鞭梢，转了几圈，随即挥出。被吊着的人惨叫起来，背上裂开一道豁口，从一侧肋骨尖横贯到另一侧，下面的肌肉和脂肪都翻了出来。{#1}苦修者{/#1}又抽一鞭，再一鞭，再一鞭。鲜血溅到苦修者身上，那个亵弄母马的家伙早已昏了过去。终于，一人站起来，夺回鞭子。

units.source: The forest is no friend of man which is why men of ill-repute sure love to put their keepsakes there. And today you've stumbled across one: a cache that {#1}Otherbrother{/#1} found by way of stubbing his toe on the edge of it. Digging out the crate and cracking it open, you find an assortment of weapons, armor, and gold. You clap the sellsword on the shoulder and thank him for his 'hard work'. He wags his boot around.
units.zh: 森林对人并不友善，所以名声不好的人偏爱把家当藏在这里。今天你们就撞见了一处：{#1}一名弟兄{/#1}的脚趾踢到箱沿，发现了藏匿点。挖出木箱撬开，里面有各式武器、护甲与金币。你拍拍佣兵的肩膀，感谢他的“辛勤劳动”。他晃了晃靴子。

units.source: You come across the once-caravan hand, {#1}Caravanhand{/#1}, finicking with the company wagon. He's nailing a slat of board to the bed and using pins to put it on a roller. The board can then drop down into the belly of the wagon with a little bit of a pull and switch. Rather ingenious. This will allow you to load more onto the wagon.

units.source: {#1}Fatguy{/#1}, once a lumbering lump of belly fat on two legs, has lost a considerable amount of weight since he's with the company. No longer does the mere notion of a sparring fight leave him without breath. In fact, he's got more bounce in his step and is showing a sort of agility you've never seen from him before. Looks like all this walking about has done wonders.
units.zh: {#1}那位曾经肥胖的弟兄{/#1}过去简直是两条腿驮着一大团赘肉，自从加入战团，已经瘦了不少。如今，他不再光想到要比划几招就喘不上气，走路甚至轻快起来，还展现出了你从未见过的灵活。看来，天天跋涉还真有奇效。

units.source: You find {#1}Glutton{/#1} helping himself to a third helping of food. That's far too much and so you demand that it be his last. Another brother joins in, mocking the man for his habits. The glutton, enraged, slams his food down and stands up. His stomach however, sways at a different pace than the rest of him and the rather fattened man goes down in a heap of flailing limbs. While the rest of the company has a laugh, you can't help but wonder if the sellsword really has gotten too fat.
units.zh: 你发现{#1}贪吃的弟兄{/#1}已经在拿第三份饭。这未免太多，你勒令他吃完这份就停。另一个弟兄也凑过来，嘲笑他的贪吃。那贪吃的家伙怒气上涌，把食物一摔，霍然起身；可肚皮晃动的节奏却跟身体其余部分不合拍，这个明显发福的家伙顿时手脚乱舞，摔成一团。全团都在笑，你却不禁琢磨，他是不是确实太胖了。

units.source: {#1}Strong1{/#1} and {#2}Strong2{/#2} - the strongest men in the outfit by some measure - are apparently undertaking something of a competition to see who is the better. You watch as they carry enormous stones from one side of an ad hoc competitive ground to the other. Then they take turns seeing how far they can throw these very stones. And then they roll the stones up a nearby hill. And then they see who can completely bury a stone the fastest.
units.zh: {#1}壮汉甲{/#1}和{#2}壮汉乙{/#2}算得上战团里力气最大的两人，此刻似乎正比试谁更强。你看着他们把巨石从临时划出的场地一头搬到另一头，接着轮流将同样的石头掷出去，看谁扔得更远。随后，他们又把石头推上附近的山坡，再比谁能最快挖坑将石头埋得严严实实。

units.source: {#1}Dumb{/#1} is perhaps one of the dumbest individuals you've ever met but, for a brief moment, it does appear that {#2}Bright{/#2} gets through and teaches him a thing or two about critical thinking and memorization. You watch as the two sit together and look over some scrolls. You're not sure where the smart man got such papers, but the unlearning oaf is certainly paying a lot of attention to them.
units.zh: {#1}迟钝的弟兄{/#1}大概是你见过最笨的人之一。不过，眼下似乎真有那么一刻，{#2}聪慧的弟兄{/#2}把道理讲进了他的脑袋，教会了他一点思考和记忆的方法。你看见两人坐在一起，翻看几卷文书。你不清楚那个聪明人从哪儿弄来这些东西，不过这不开窍的笨蛋，确实看得很专心。

units.source: As you watch, {#1}Dumb{/#1} is asking rather deep, profound questions. Questions about the land and its relationship to people, and the sky and its relationship to the birds. You slowly realize the idiot is merely glancing around and describing what he's seeing in the sort of 'inquisitive' language {#2}Bright{/#2} has taught him - namely by attaching a smarmily-intoned question to the end of every sentence. When the two finish up, {#3}Bright{/#3} comes to you with a grin.
units.zh: 你在旁观察，发现{#1}迟钝的弟兄{/#1}竟接连提出深奥的问题：土地与人的关系，天空与鸟的关系。慢慢地，你才明白，这傻瓜不过是在环顾四周，把看见的东西套进{#2}聪慧的弟兄{/#2}教他的“探究”语气里——也就是每说一句话，便自作聪明地添个问句。等两人学完，{#3}聪慧的弟兄{/#3}笑着来找你。

units.source: {#1}Cultist{/#1} the cultist gets up and looks at the sun. As he continues to stare at it, a shadow slowly emerges over his face, as though some entity were shielding him from the light. Suddenly, he raises a hand and starts drawing some aerial rites with his hand. You swear the darkness on his face is moving as though an imprint of his drawings, a sort of shifting tattoo. When he's finished, he takes a seat.
units.zh: {#1}邪教徒{/#1}站起来，望向太阳。他一直盯着，脸上却渐渐浮出阴影，仿佛有某种存在替他挡住了光。忽然，他抬手在空中划起仪式符号。你敢发誓，他脸上的黑暗正随手势变化，像一幅不断移动的刺青。做完，他重新坐下。

units.source: "{#1}Bastard{/#1} has an army waiting for him if he so chooses. That's why the nobles want him dead, because he stands as a real and viable threat to the status quo and this he does not yet know. I suppose he doesn't have to, either, but it'd be a nice send off, no? You get to see to it that his place in this world is justified and that he isn't some accident gliding through a world he believes to hate him. But what about me, a grossly talented assassin with a perfect streak of kills, hm? What about me? Well, I don't want this life anymore. So here's my offer: I take his place. He goes home, I go with you. He goes and conquers, my benefactors are nonethewiser and for all they know, I simply disappeared. Sounds good, no?"
units.zh: "只要{#1}私生子{/#1}愿意，就有一支军队等着他。这才是贵族想杀他的原因：他真能动摇他们眼下的地位，只是他自己还不知道。当然，他也不必知道。可给他这样的前程，岂不是一场体面的送别？你可以让他明白，他在这世上自有一席之地，并非一次意外留下的孽种，也不必觉得整个世界都恨他。那我呢？我这么一个本领高强、从未失手的刺客，该怎么办，嗯？说到底，我不想再过这种日子了。我的条件是：我顶替他。他回家，我跟你走。他去打天下，我的雇主蒙在鼓里，只当我凭空消失。听起来不错吧？"

units.source: {#1}Bastard{/#1} deserves better. Not that the {#2}Companyname{/#2} is beneath him, but he is a man who has spent his whole life seeing himself as an outsider, a blight upon his own family name, a threat to those he love merely because they carry a finer bloodline than he. You agree to the assassin's demand and send for the bastard to enter your tent. When he does, you quickly explain the situation. He asks for proof that an army is awaiting him and the hired killer quickly complies, producing a stamped scroll with a sigil and signature only the bastard could recognize. {#3}Bastard{/#3} reads it carefully. He lowers and looks to you.
units.zh: {#1}私生子{/#1}值得更好的前程。并非{#2}〈战团名〉{/#2}配不上他，只是他一辈子都把自己当成局外人、家族姓氏上的污点。仅因血统不及那些所爱的人高贵，他的存在便成了对他们的威胁。你答应刺客的条件，派人叫私生子进帐篷。他一来，你便简要说明情况。他要求证明真有一支军队在等他，那受雇的杀手马上取出一卷盖了印的文书，上面的徽记与签名，只有私生子认得。{#3}私生子{/#3}仔细读完，放下卷轴，看着你。

And then he leaves. Turning around, you find the assassin bowing.

You hear a commotion outside and rush to it. {#1}Bastard{/#1} the bastard is laying on the ground, a few other brothers beside him. {#2}Otherbrother{/#2} comes over to ask if you're okay. units.source: "Out in {#1}Randomtown{/#1} they had a father up for trial. He'd murdered two brothers on account of knocking his cart over. And then apparently the taste of it had him murdering some more. All told, he took the lives of at least seven people. Naturally, they hanged the man. But I ran into his son the other day and he told me the hanging was merely some clerical mistake. His father was an upstanding man, not the least bit self-serving and the people he killed had it coming. What's more curious, this youngin' is now mayor! Now, the way I remember it the man slaughtered seven folks outright. Just like that! But last time I was in town they'd moved his long-necked bones to a proper cemetery and I'll be damned if I didn't see some flowers on the tombstone. Not sure what to make of these things."
units.zh: "{#1}〈城镇名〉{/#1}那边，曾经审过一个当爹的。他杀了一对兄弟，就因为人家碰翻了他的货车。后来大概是杀出了滋味，又接着杀人。算下来，至少有七条人命。那当然得把他吊死。可前几天，我碰见了他的儿子，那小子竟说，他爹被绞死，只是文书上弄错了。他爹为人正直，半点私心也没有，那些被杀的人全是活该。更怪的是，这年轻人如今竟当上了镇长！我记得清清楚楚，那人就是把七个人杀了，说杀就杀！可上次进城，我发现他们把那具脖子吊长了的尸骨迁进了正经墓地，墓碑上甚至还摆着鲜花，骗你我是狗。这些事，我真不知道该怎么想。"

units.source: "I saw'r man cut down by lightning a few months ago. {#1}Randomname{/#1} was his name. He had a lumber mill for a mouth, a wooden bite from side-to-side. Termites for teeth we used to say! Anyway, I'd found his head aflame, grinning hot fire back at me, his flesh curled down in strips of black and purple. The ground around him was scorched, smoke drifting around and little fires crackling. But he was still alive. So I ran off to get some help when I heard a horrid noise behind me. Damned lightning struck him again! Smote by the gods through and through."
units.zh: "几个月前，我见过一个人被雷劈倒。他叫{#1}〈人名〉{/#1}。他那张嘴简直是个锯木厂，满口上下都是木头假牙，咱们总说，他长的是一嘴白蚁！总之，我发现他时，他脑袋上正烧着火，冲我咧嘴一笑，嘴里也是热焰。皮肉焦黑发紫，成条地卷了下来。周围地面烧焦了，烟气飘着，几簇小火噼啪作响。可他还活着。我便跑去找人帮忙，谁知身后又传来一声巨响。该死的雷居然又劈中了他！诸神这是非要把他劈个透啊。"

units.source: "Out in {#1}Randomtown{/#1} they hanged a boy for killin' a merchant. Said he threw a stone at the trader to knock him off his cart. He then ran over to steal his things, but the stoned man wasn't knocked out, so he drew his dagger and the boy drew his and I guess the boy was the one left standing when it was all said and done, o'course, he now just be left swinging. Talk of the execution say he kicked good and long, wouldn't stop kicking even after he was dead. Maybe his cold feet were lookin' for warmth."

units.source: Climbing and barreling through the ups and downs of the mountain range has tested the men as well as any foe. While the company is a little worse for the wear, they have been made better by the rigors and trials of the harsh landscape - {#1}Dude{/#1} most of all.
units.zh: 在起伏的群山中攀爬奔走，对弟兄们的考验不亚于任何敌人。战团虽有些疲惫狼狈，却也被这片险峻大地的艰苦磨炼得更强了，尤其是{#1}某位弟兄{/#1}。

units.source: As the men wander through {#1}Townname{/#1} looking for things to do, {#2}Juggler{/#2} the juggler takes it upon himself to provide his own entertainment. He takes a message barker's scroll and folds it into a paper hat with horns. Placing it upon his head, he then glides into a crowd of peasants and asks for anything with which to juggle. They toss him all manner of objects from carrots to knives and one man even offers a newborn infant before the mother slaps him for even suggesting it. Whatever is thrown up there, the juggler easily hurls through the air, his own body twisting and turning, his feet alternating between hands to kick things back into the air. It's dexterous poetry in motion - and a boon for the town's downtrodden. You get the feeling that the juggler has represented the {#3}Companyname{/#3} well this day.
units.zh: 弟兄们在{#1}〈城镇名〉{/#1}闲逛找乐子，{#2}杂耍艺人{/#2}索性自己找起了乐。他拿过传令人的卷轴，折成一顶长角的纸帽戴上，轻快地钻进农民堆里，讨要任何能拿来抛接的东西。人们扔来胡萝卜、刀子，五花八门；甚至有人想递上刚出生的婴儿，才一提议，就被孩子母亲扇了一巴掌。不管抛来的是什么，艺人都能轻巧地让它在空中翻飞。他转身扭腰，手脚交替接物，再用脚将东西踢回半空。动作灵巧得如同一首活的诗，也让镇上那些愁苦的人得了片刻欢乐。你觉得，今天他着实替{#3}〈战团名〉{/#3}挣了个好名声。

provenance.game_source: As the men wander through %townname% looking for things to do, %juggler% the juggler takes it upon himself to provide his own entertainment. He takes a message barker's scroll and folds it into a paper hat with horns. Placing it upon his head, he then glides into a crowd of peasants and asks for anything with which to juggle. They toss him all manner of objects from carrots to knives and one man even offers a newborn infant before the mother slaps him for even suggesting it. Whatever is thrown up there, the juggler easily hurls through the air, his own body twisting and turning, his feet alternating between hands to kick things back into the air. It's dexterous poetry in motion - and a boon for the town's downtrodden. You get the feeling that the juggler has represented the %companyname% well this day.

units.source: {#1}Farmhand{/#1} and {#2}Fisherman{/#2} are having a bit of an arm-wrestling contest. It's all in good fun, having apparently been borne out of an argument on whether fishermen or farmers are more important or whose food is best, that which walks the land or that which swims the oceans. With a long, salty belch, and singing with praise for some long-lost whale, the fisherman puts the last of his strength into the bout and pins {#3}Farmhand{/#3}'s arm. Both men get up and clap one another on the shoulders.
units.zh: {#1}农场帮工{/#1}与{#2}渔夫{/#2}正在掰腕子。两人玩得开心，起因似乎是争论渔夫和农夫谁更重要，以及地上走的和海里游的，究竟哪种更好吃。渔夫打了个悠长、满是海腥味的嗝，又唱起歌，赞颂一头不知失踪多久的鲸鱼，最后使足力气，将{#3}农场帮工{/#3}的手臂压倒。两人站起来，互相拍了拍肩膀。

units.zh: 你摇摇头，问那女巫想要什么。{#1}迷信的弟兄{/#1}说，要400克朗，否则这诅咒就得跟他一辈子。

units.source: He says he can indeed lend a hand for the old gods are always at war with the evils of witchcraft and other sorcery. Before he goes off on a long monologue about this old god or that one, you dip away and send him {#1}Superstitious{/#1}. For a few minutes, there is peace and quiet in your tent. But you know it can't last, for you are like a man beneath a rockslide, awaiting the tumbling stone with his name on it.
units.zh: 他说自己确实有办法：旧神向来与巫术及各种邪法势不两立。他正要长篇大论地讲起这位神、那位神，你便溜开了，把{#1}迷信的弟兄{/#1}打发过去。接下来的几分钟，帐篷里安安静静。可你知道，这太平维持不了多久。你就像站在山崩之下的人，等着那块专冲自己砸来的石头。

units.source: The company sits around a fire when {#1}Minstrel{/#1} the minstrel notices the refugee, {#2}Refugee{/#2}, sitting solemnly by himself. Within but a moment, the minstrel is on his feet, standing high on a stump, and waving his arms wide.

units.source: "Lo', the town of {#1}Refugee{/#1} was small, its place quaint, and its food, well, a little on the 'eh' side. But ho'! Were its people big! For here sits amongst our company one of its kin, the world after his spirit, death on his heels, yet here he be, and we've but only thanks - and crowns! - to offer him! Such is the price of his company, and such we are willing to give."
units.zh: "诸位且听！{#1}难民{/#1}的家乡是座小镇，地方古朴，吃食嘛，稍稍有点……一言难尽。可嘿！那里的人却何等了不起！如今就有一位坐在咱们中间，世道要磨灭他的斗志，死神在身后紧追不舍，可他依然活着，来到了这里！咱们能献上的唯有感谢——还有克朗！能得他相伴，这份酬劳咱们付得心甘情愿。"

units.source: You find {#1}Oldguard{/#1} nursing a rather large tankard next to a fire. In fact, it's not a tankard at all, but a wooden bucket filled with ale. A few more modest mugs are littered about his feet. He tips back, gulping from the bucket's lip. When he sees you, he tries to dress up, sloughing the foam off his face and attempting a smile that quickly sloops into a drunken frown.
units.zh: 你发现{#1}老兵{/#1}坐在火边，抱着一个大得出奇的酒杯慢慢喝。其实，那根本不是酒杯，而是一只盛满麦酒的木桶。他脚边还散落着几个大小正常的杯子。他仰起头，凑着桶沿大口吞咽。见你走来，他试图收拾仪容，抹去脸上的酒沫，勉强挤出一笑，却很快又皱成一张醉醺醺的苦脸。

units.source: "Like shit. That's how I'm feeling. First, {#1}Casualty{/#1} went down. Then {#2}Othercasualty{/#2}. I know there's been at least five or six others. Just dead men. Come and gone. I got memories of them talking, and memories of them screaming, and I can't have one without the other. But I'm alright now cause right now I can't even think straight. If I can't unlearn a memory, I'll just go ahead and drown it. The ale does me well, heh."
units.zh: "糟透了。这就是我的感觉。先是{#1}弟兄甲{/#1}倒下了，然后是{#2}弟兄乙{/#2}。我知道，至少还有五六个。全死了。来了，又没了。我记得他们说话，也记得他们惨叫。一想起这个，另一个就跟着来了。不过，现在我没事，因为现在我连想都想不清楚。既然没法忘掉，我就把那些记忆全泡死在酒里。麦酒对我挺好，嘿。"

units.source: While traversing the snowy wastelands of the realm's north, {#1}Houndmaster{/#1} the houndmaster has come to befriend a creature that's been trailing beside the company's march: a wolf. The houndmaster frequently remained in the rearguard, crouched low, hands at his side, locking eyes with the lone wolf for minutes on end. But today, using a bit of leftover meat, he plied the beast right into the middle of the camp. Now he squats at its side, dwarfed by its prominent, muscled withers, its pointed and attentive ears, and a lapping maw lined with mankilling canines.
units.zh: 穿越北方冰雪荒原时，{#1}驯犬师{/#1}渐渐与一头始终尾随战团的野兽交上了朋友：一匹狼。他常留在队尾，压低身子，双手垂在身侧，与那匹孤狼对视，一看就是好几分钟。可今天，他竟用一点剩肉，将它一路引进了营地中央。如今，他蹲在狼身边，在它高耸而强健的肩背、竖起警觉的双耳，以及不断舔动、长满夺命獠牙的大嘴旁，显得小了许多。

units.source: While relaxing after the day's walk, {#1}Gambler{/#1} comes up to you with a pair of dice and a cup in hand. He asks if you wish to have a little game. The rules are quite simple: you roll the dice from the cup, whoever has the highest numbers wins. It's pure chance! The wager will be twenty-five crowns per dice roll.

units.source: {#1}Spartan{/#1} has always been a bit tight with how much he eats. You're not sure if it's part of some religious rite, a sense of duty, or he's just not a big eater. Regardless, the lack of food has weakened the man and you find him barely able to sit upright on a log. You've got a bowl of meat and corn in hand, wondering if maybe you should offer it to him.
units.zh: {#1}节省口粮的弟兄{/#1}吃东西一向很克制。你不清楚这是宗教习俗、责任感，还是单纯饭量小。总之，吃得不足已让他虚弱不堪，如今连在原木上坐直都费劲。你手里端着一碗肉和玉米，琢磨着是不是该给他。

units.source: Stairs lead you to the pits where a crowd huddles around a makeshift arena of dirt and wobbly fenceposts. The action can't be seen yet, but off to the side are a pile of dead dogs and beside them sit their killers, eyes wild, blood frothing mouths agape in horrified panting. As two dogs clash in the arena, you glance at {#1}Doghandler{/#1}.
units.zh: 你沿楼梯向下，来到斗犬场。人群挤在用泥地和摇晃木桩围成的简陋场地四周。你还看不见场内的厮斗，却先看见旁边堆着一摞死狗。杀死它们的狗就坐在一旁，眼神狂乱，张着满是血沫的嘴，惊魂未定地喘息。场内两条狗扑到一起时，你转头看了看{#1}带犬的弟兄{/#1}。

units.source: Its eyes dart around and as its shoulder rests against your pantleg, you can feel a quickening heartbeat. Across from you stands your competition: a scummy looking doghandler and a massive beast more wolf than dog. The mutt is missing its bottom lip, displaying a jagged row of teeth that have been chiseled to be deadlier than they already are. Scabs and sores mottle its crooked body, but the musculature of its frame is apparent and {#1}Doghandler{/#1} whispers that this will be ugly.
units.zh: 它的目光四处乱转，肩膀贴着你的裤腿，你能感觉到它越来越急促的心跳。对面站着你的对手：一个满脸龌龊相的驯犬人，还有一头与其说是狗、不如说更像狼的巨兽。那杂种狗的下唇没了，露出参差的尖牙，牙齿还被刻意凿尖，显得更加致命。它扭曲的身躯遍布痂疤与烂疮，可浑身肌肉依然清晰可见。{#1}带犬的弟兄{/#1}低声说，这场面怕是会很难看。

provenance.method: Independently reviewed exact game variable template
provenance.game_source: Its eyes dart around and as its shoulder rests against your pantleg, you can feel a quickening heartbeat. Across from you stands your competition: a scummy looking doghandler and a massive beast more wolf than dog. The mutt is missing its bottom lip, displaying a jagged row of teeth that have been chiseled to be deadlier than they already are. Scabs and sores mottle its crooked body, but the musculature of its frame is apparent and %doghandler% whispers that this will be ugly.

units.source: {#1}Wardog{/#1} yips and jabs forward, the mongrel bred with war in him, and with an outstretched hand you unleash your hound just as your opponent does his.
units.zh: {#1}战犬{/#1}吠了一声，猛地向前挣去，血脉中的斗性已被唤醒。你伸出手，松开了猎犬，对方也在同一刻放开了他的狗。

units.source: The two dogs sprint toward one another and cover the small arena in a flash. They collide, their crude bodies wheeling away from one another before their feet plant and charge in for another shot. The opponent's dog ducks beneath {#1}Wardog{/#1} then rises back up, glomming onto the underside of your dog's neck.
units.zh: 两条狗相向疾冲，转眼便跨过狭小的斗场。它们迎面撞上，粗壮的身躯各自翻滚开，随即四爪落地，再次扑向彼此。对手的狗钻到{#1}战犬{/#1}下方，猛地抬头，死死咬住你战犬的喉咙下侧。

units.source: {#1}Doghandler{/#1}'s hands go to his face, his eyes staring out between his fingers. You watch as {#2}Wardog{/#2} is shaken from side to side. Blood spurts from its nose as it yelps. You can hear the scratch of scissoring, helpless legs as the dog tries to kick across the dirt. The audience jeers and laughs.

units.source: The two dogs sprint across the arena. {#1}Wardog{/#1} goes high, and its opponent low. You watch in horror as the opponent's mutt shoots up from its low stance and clamps its jaws under {#2}Wardog{/#2}'s neck. They tumble across the arena and in the violent momentum {#3}Wardog{/#3}'s throat is ripped clean out. Blood sprays so fiercely that the audience jumps back to get away. The victorious mongrel returns to its owner and drops a rag of flesh and muscle at his feet.
units.zh: 两条狗飞奔着冲过场地。{#1}战犬{/#1}高高跃起，对手却压低身子。你惊恐地看着那条杂种狗从低处猛然蹿起，一口扣住{#2}战犬{/#2}的颈下。它们在场中翻滚，猛烈的冲势将{#3}战犬{/#3}的喉咙整个扯了出来。鲜血喷涌得如此凶猛，观众纷纷向后跳开躲避。得胜的狗回到主人身边，把一团撕碎的皮肉丢在他脚下。

units.source: {#1}Wardog{/#1} stumbles across the dirt. It retches for breath, its throat puckering and wheezing and gargling. {#2}Doghandler{/#2} jumps the fence and kneels beside the mutt. He tries to cover the wound, but it's no use. The dog stares at you as it dies.
units.zh: {#1}战犬{/#1}在泥地上踉跄着走了几步，拼命想要呼吸，喉部的伤口一缩一张，发出嘶哑的咕噜声。{#2}带犬的弟兄{/#2}翻过围栏，跪在它身旁，试图捂住伤口，却无济于事。它望着你，咽下了最后一口气。

units.source: {#1}Wardog{/#1} drives its opponent into a fence post. You watch as your dog buries its jaws into its opponent's face, jamming its teeth through an eye in one bite, and taking a chunk of tongue in another. The defeated mutt is bitten to pieces, literally, and as it falls in defeat your dog commits to a throat-ripping execution.
units.zh: {#1}战犬{/#1}把对手顶到一根围栏木桩上。你看着它咬住对手的脸，一口刺穿眼睛，又一口扯掉了半截舌头。那条败犬被咬得支离破碎；等它倒下，你的狗便一口撕开它的喉咙，结束了性命。

units.source: Your opponent cries out and tries to jump the fence, but the audience reels him back. {#1}Doghandler{/#1} pats you on the back.
units.zh: 对手哀叫着想翻进围栏，却被观众拖了回去。{#1}带犬的弟兄{/#1}拍了拍你的背。

units.source: You decide not to intervene, instead letting {#1}Wardog{/#1}'s fight, and potential demise, go where it may. The choice is soon rewarded: you watch as your dog gets its hind paws against one of the fenceposts circling the arena. With a good kick it manages to slide itself underneath its combatant and there tear out the dangling testicles in a disgusting display of survivalism. The poor emasculated mongrel, shrieking, wheels around only to put its neck directly into the jaws of {#2}Wardog{/#2}. The fight ends quickly, and almost mercifully, from there.
units.zh: 你决定不插手，任由{#1}战犬{/#1}继续搏斗，哪怕它可能就此丧命。这个决定很快有了回报：你看见自己的狗用后爪抵住场边的一根木桩，猛地一蹬，滑到了对手腹下，随即扯下了垂着的睾丸。这求生的手段恶心得令人作呕。可怜的杂种狗惨叫着转过身，却正好将脖子送进{#2}战犬{/#2}的嘴里。接下来的厮杀很快便结束了，快得几乎称得上仁慈。

units.source: You go to collect your reward while {#1}Doghandler{/#1} hugs the now tail-wagging {#2}Wardog{/#2}.
units.zh: 你去领取赢来的钱，{#1}带犬的弟兄{/#1}则抱住了已经开始摇尾巴的{#2}战犬{/#2}。

provenance.method: Independently reviewed exact game variable template

units.source: You don't intervene and even have to hold back {#1}Doghandler{/#1} as the man tries to jump the fence. The two of you can only watch in horror as the fierce mongrel's snapping bites tear away at {#2}Wardog{/#2}'s face piece by piece. Soon, your dog sinks to the ground, giving up its neck. Bloody tearing follows suit and {#3}Wardog{/#3} is very quickly a dead dog. Distraught, {#4}Doghandler{/#4} can only sink to the ground and cover his face.
units.zh: 你没有干涉，甚至还拉住了想翻过围栏的{#1}带犬的弟兄{/#1}。你们只能惊恐地看着那凶悍的杂种狗连连撕咬，将{#2}战犬{/#2}的脸一块块扯烂。很快，你的狗倒在地上，暴露出脖子。紧接着又是一阵血肉撕裂，{#3}战犬{/#3}转眼便断了气。{#4}带犬的弟兄{/#4}悲痛欲绝，瘫坐在地，双手捂住脸。

units.source: With a quick leap you jump the fence and run into the arena. {#1}Doghandler{/#1} is right behind you. The two dogs are still at it, but a swift kick gets them separated. The houndmaster quickly grabs {#2}Wardog{/#2} and lifts him out of danger. The crowd boos and bottles and glasses start flying in. A man blows a whistle that silences them all. He steps into the arena.
units.zh: 你一跃翻过围栏，冲进斗犬场，{#1}带犬的弟兄{/#1}紧随其后。两条狗还在撕咬，你猛踢一脚，将它们分开。驯犬师赶紧抱起{#2}战犬{/#2}，把它带离险境。人群嘘声四起，酒瓶和杯子纷纷砸了过来。一个男人吹响哨子，让所有人安静下来，随后走进场内。

units.source: You take out {#1}Demand{/#1} crowns and hand them over. The crowd boos, but the man in charge blows his whistle again.
units.zh: 你取出{#1}〈索要的金额〉{/#1}克朗交过去。人群发出嘘声，管事的又吹响哨子。

provenance.method: Independently reviewed exact game variable template

units.source: The crowd pipes down. You start to leave, {#1}Doghandler{/#1} behind you with an unconscious {#2}Wardog{/#2} strung limply across his arms. A few patrons hiss and spit, but that's about the most they do and you're perfectly fine with that.
units.zh: 人群安静下来。你转身离开，{#1}带犬的弟兄{/#1}跟在后面，昏迷的{#2}战犬{/#2}软绵绵地横在他臂弯里。有些看客仍嘘叫、吐口水，可也仅此而已；这样已经很好了。

units.source: You order {#1}Doghandler{/#1} to put the dog down. His eyes widen.
units.zh: 你命令{#1}带犬的弟兄{/#1}把狗放下。他瞪大眼睛。

provenance.method: Independently reviewed exact game variable template
provenance.game_source: You order %doghandler% to put the dog down. His eyes widen.

units.source: Nodding, you say you are. {#1}Wardog{/#1}'s barely awake, snorting between frightened alertness and deadened unconsciousness. When {#2}Doghandler{/#2} hesitates again, you grab the dog and pull it away. You nod to the crowd, and then to your opponent who unleashes his murderous hound a second time. {#3}Wardog{/#3}'s weary, watery eyes look up at you, blink, then close. You put the dog down and your opponent's hound descend upon it with bestial fury. You try not to listen to the horrific demise unfolding at your feet.
units.zh: 你点头，表示自己是认真的。{#1}战犬{/#1}几乎已醒不过来，喷着鼻息，在惊恐的清醒与麻木的昏迷间挣扎。见{#2}带犬的弟兄{/#2}再次迟疑，你一把接过狗，将它拉开。你朝人群点头，又向对手示意。对方第二次放出了那条凶狠的猎犬。{#3}战犬{/#3}用疲倦、含泪的眼睛望着你，眨了一下，随后闭上。你将狗放到地上，对手的猎犬立刻带着兽性的狂暴扑了上来。你尽量不去听，脚边那场可怕的死亡正在发出的声响。

units.source: A shadow crosses over you from behind. When you look back, {#1}Brawler{/#1} is standing there with a rather distant look in his eyes. He cracks his knuckles in one long staccato before asking if he can train up {#2}Trainee{/#2}. You ask why. The brawler looks down at you.
units.zh: 一片阴影从身后罩住你。你回头，发现{#1}拳斗者{/#1}站在那里，目光有些出神。他把指节掰得接连作响，随后问你，能不能让他操练操练{#2}受训的弟兄{/#2}。你问为什么。拳斗者低头看着你。

units.source: {#1}Brawler{/#1} and {#2}Trainee{/#2} are found in a mudpit with their hands wrapped in cloth and leaves, padding for the knuckles and to keep them from cutting one another with every punch. The brawler has his trainee bouncing counter-clockwise along the ring of the fighting circle, punching the air as he goes, and with his trainer hitting or kicking him every time he passes by. The men glisten with sweat as they work. When {#3}Trainee{/#3} begins to slow, {#4}Brawler{/#4} hits him as though a jockey would a sluggish horse.
units.zh: 你看见{#1}拳斗者{/#1}与{#2}受训的弟兄{/#2}站在泥地里，双手缠着布条和树叶，给指节垫上一层，免得拳拳都把对方打得皮开肉绽。拳斗者让徒弟沿着圈子逆时针蹦跳，一边移动一边对空挥拳。每次从师父面前经过，还得挨上一拳或一脚。两人练得汗光淋漓。只要{#3}受训的弟兄{/#3}稍一慢下来，{#4}拳斗者{/#4}就像骑手抽打懒马一样，打他一下。

units.source: After an hour of this, {#1}Brawler{/#1} steps back and invites his trainee to attack him. Predictably, the assault is aimless and pitiful. Long, looping punches are thrown with no energy behind them. The brawler ducks and weaves out of the way, punching every attempted strike with a counter-punch of his own.
units.zh: 练了一小时，{#1}拳斗者{/#1}退后，示意徒弟攻过来。不出所料，进攻既杂乱，又可怜。拳头抡得老远，却半点劲道也没有。拳斗者左闪右避，每躲过一次攻击，便还上一记反击。

units.source: The brawler has {#1}Trainee{/#1} stand completely still. He circles about the man, cracking his knuckles as he sizes him up. Finally, he lets his intentions be known.
units.zh: 拳斗者让{#1}受训的弟兄{/#1}站定不动。他绕着对方打转，一边掰响指节，一边上下打量。终于，他说出了自己的打算。

units.source: A moment is given to the trainee to acknowledge what is about to happen. He sucks in a great gulp of breath and then nods. {#1}Brawler{/#1} wastes no time wheeling a bola punch right into the man's chest. He bowls over at which point he is kicked in the shoulder repeatedly until he stands back up.
units.zh: 他给徒弟留了片刻，好让他明白即将发生什么。那人深吸一口气，点点头。{#1}拳斗者{/#1}毫不耽搁，抡起一记重拳，正中胸口。徒弟弯腰倒下，又挨了好几脚踢在肩上，直到重新爬起来。

units.source: {#1}Brawler{/#1} the heavy-handed-rough-and-tumble brawler is found leaning over, his arms fenced out before himself in a defensive posture, and {#2}Trainee{/#2} is standing adjacent, trying to mimic the stance. units.source: The brawler ignores the question and simply asks the man to attack him. {#1}Trainee{/#1} obliges, coming in high with a hurled fist. {#2}Brawler{/#2} deflects the blow with a shoulder-roll before throwing a cross-counter that has {#3}Trainee{/#3} spinning on his feet. units.source: It's not a rare sight to find a dead body on your journey. This one, though, is rather unusual. {#1}Randombrother{/#1} takes a long look.
units.zh: 旅途中见到尸体，并不稀奇，可这一具实在古怪。{#1}某位弟兄{/#1}盯着看了许久。

provenance.game_source: It's not a rare sight to find a dead body on your journey. This one, though, is rather unusual. %randombrother% takes a long look.

units.source: You crouch down and throw back the corpse's shirt. Scars run lengthwise all about his body, drawn in very familiar shapes: forests, rivers, mountains. {#1}Randombrother{/#1} walks up.
units.zh: 你蹲下，掀开死者的衣服。长长的伤疤遍布全身，刻出的形状十分眼熟：森林、河流、山脉。{#1}某位弟兄{/#1}走上前。

units.source: As you follow the foosteps, you begin to hear the murmurs of a chant. You tell the company to rest while you sneak forward, eventually finding a large bonfire with cloaked men circling around it. They stomp their feet and throw their hands up, shouting some token words to their elder god, Davkul. It's a bestial ceremony, roaring and growling abound, and the men dance about with their oversized clothes like darkly spirits still angry at the world they'd departed. {#1}Randombrother{/#1} crawls up beside you and shakes his head.
units.zh: 沿脚印前行，你渐渐听见低沉的吟诵声。你让战团停下，自己悄悄上前，终于看见一大堆篝火，披袍的人们围着它转圈。他们跺脚、举手，向那古老的神祇达夫库尔高喊着仪式用语。这场典礼满是兽性，咆哮与低吼此起彼伏。人们裹着宽大的衣袍舞动，像一群死后仍怨恨人间的幽魂。{#1}某位弟兄{/#1}爬到你身边，摇着头。

units.source: You ask {#1}Cultist{/#1} if he can do anything. He simply walks past you and down the hill. The group of cultists turn and look to him. He walks through the crowd to the prisoner. They talk. He whispers, the prisoner nods. When they finish, the {#2}Cultist{/#2} nods to the crowd of cultists. One member steps forward, disrobes, and pitches himself into the fire, screamless and without protest. Another cultist pitches a rake into the flames, tearing something out of it and handing it over to {#3}Cultist{/#3}. The prisoner, his life ostensibly spared in an exchange, is freed and you watch as {#4}Cultist{/#4} grabs him and takes him back up the hill. He pushes the man forward as he speaks.
units.zh: 你问{#1}邪教徒{/#1}有没有办法。他径直从你身边走过，下了山坡。教徒们转身看着他。他穿过人群，来到囚徒面前。两人交谈起来，他低声说着什么，囚徒点头。谈完，{#2}邪教徒{/#2}朝教徒们点了点头。一个人走出队列，脱去衣袍，投身火中，既无惨叫，也无抗拒。另一名教徒把耙子伸进火焰，扯出一件东西，递给{#3}邪教徒{/#3}。囚徒被解开锁链，看来是以另一条命换得了生还。你看着{#4}邪教徒{/#4}拉住他，带回山坡。教徒把人往前一推，说道。

units.source: You ask what it is he has in his hand. The cultist holds up what had been retrieved from the flames. It is a skull patched over in leathered flesh, and stretched taut over its face is a freshly singed visage, presumably of the man who had tossed himself into the fire. Slight hints of his face twist and turn, his mouth wringed ajar, misshapen by a cruel and murmuring darkness. Still holding it aloft like a native showing off a prized scalp, {#1}Cultist{/#1} speaks bluntly.
units.zh: 你问他手里拿着什么。他举起刚从火中取出的东西：一块裹着皮革般血肉的头骨，脸部绷着一张刚被烧焦的面皮，想来属于投火的那个人。依稀可辨的五官扭曲抽动，嘴巴被拧得张开，残酷而低语不止的黑暗将它歪曲成异形。{#1}邪教徒{/#1}像展示珍贵头皮的部族人一样高举着它，直截了当地说。

units.source: You find the nobleman {#1}Nobleman{/#1} and the rather ragged-looking {#2}Lowborn{/#2} quarreling over the last piece of food on a spit. Apparently the lowborn got his fork to it first, but the nobleman claimed that his high stature granted him the right to the meat.

units.source: The sellsword crouches before the dog and without pause puts its hands around the scuff of its neck and starts to scratch. Despite the sudden movements, the dog responds positively and when the man stops scratching the dog lifts up off the ground and lopes forward and follows the man. {#1}Houndman{/#1} stares back at you as he roughs the dog up with some heavy petting.
units.zh: 他在狗面前蹲下，毫不迟疑地双手抓住它颈后的皮毛，揉搓起来。动作虽突然，那狗却很受用。他一停手，狗便从地上爬起来，小跑着跟上了他。{#1}驯犬的弟兄{/#1}一边大力揉着狗，一边回头看你。

units.source: A hint of murmuring grows louder and louder until you can no longer focus. You put your quill pen down with the sort of energy the ink bottle can take without breaking and step out of your tent. {#1}Archer1{/#1} and {#2}Archer2{/#2} are standing there bickering over who is the better shot. Seeing you, they waste little time asking if they can hold a shooting contest to decide who is right.
units.zh: 窃窃私语越来越响，终于吵得你无法专心。你重重搁下羽毛笔，力道刚好没让墨水瓶遭殃，随后走出帐篷。{#1}弓手甲{/#1}与{#2}弓手乙{/#2}正在外头争论谁射得更准。一看见你，两人立刻请求办场射术比试，分个高下。

units.source: The raider, {#1}Raider{/#1}, is sharpening his weapon beside the campfire. He tells stories of his days raiding coasts and making off with piles of loot, his crooked smile grinning in the blade's sharpened sheen. {#2}Sellsword{/#2} the sellsword listens for a time then gets up laughing.
units.zh: {#1}劫掠者{/#1}正坐在营火旁磨刀，讲着从前袭掠海岸、满载战利品而归的故事，锋利的刀面映出他歪斜的笑容。{#2}佣兵{/#2}听了一会儿，笑着站起身。

units.source: "We islanders at least have honor amongst us, whereas you'd stab the {#1}Companyname{/#1} in the back for an extra crown in your purse. Speak ill of my past again, sellsword, and I'll have that mouth of yours gnawing dirt."
units.zh: "我们岛民之间至少还讲荣誉，你却会为钱袋里多添一枚克朗，就在{#1}〈战团名〉{/#1}背后捅刀子。再敢诋毁我的过去，佣兵，我就让你这张嘴啃个满口泥。"

units.source: Carrying a leathered tome in hand, {#1}Historian{/#1} shuffles into your tent. Without a word spoken he lays the book on the table and takes a step back. You set your quill pen down and ask what it is. He says to open it. Sighing, you open the book and come to find pages littered with names and events you know well. It is a history of the company and its adventures. You flip through the pages, seeing old tales that warm the heart and some that break it. You close the book and push it back across the table. The historian asks if it is alright, and you nod. You say give it to the men to read around camp for it will surely lift their spirits.
units.zh: {#1}历史学者{/#1}捧着一本皮面厚书，缓步走进你的帐篷。他一言不发地把书放在桌上，又退开一步。你搁下羽毛笔，问这是什么。他让你翻开看看。你叹了口气，打开书，发现满纸都是自己熟悉的名字与往事。这是一本记述战团及其冒险经历的史书。你一页页翻过，有些旧事令人心头一暖，有些则令人心碎。你合上书，将它沿桌面推了回去。历史学者问写得是否还行，你点点头，让他拿给营里的弟兄们传阅，相信这一定能让大家打起精神。

units.source: Ah, the campfire is brimming with talk and chatter. The men are enjoying some beer and food when rather suddenly the shouts of two men in particular get everyone else to quiet down, not because they yell louder than the rest, but because it's rather out of character for the both of them: the monks {#1}Monk1{/#1} and {#2}Monk2{/#2} are screaming-deep in a theological debate.
units.zh: 篝火旁谈笑声不断，弟兄们喝着啤酒，吃着东西。突然，两个人的叫嚷让其他人都安静下来。并不是他们喊得最响，而是这场面实在与他们平日的模样相去甚远：{#1}修士甲{/#1}和{#2}修士乙{/#2}正为神学争论得面红耳赤。

provenance.method: Independently reviewed exact game variable template
provenance.game_source: Ah, the campfire is brimming with talk and chatter. The men are enjoying some beer and food when rather suddenly the shouts of two men in particular get everyone else to quiet down, not because they yell louder than the rest, but because it's rather out of character for the both of them: the monks %monk1% and %monk2% are screaming-deep in a theological debate.

units.source: For a moment, you think to stop the debate before it gets out of hand and into fists, but then you remember that this isn't the first time you've seen two holy men exchanging rather heatedly. It's just what they do. So you decide to let the men hash it out. In time, their voices lower in volume, and their faces lower together into a book. They quietly peruse it, bumping heads as they draw their eyes over the pages. Finally, {#1}Monk1{/#1} raises up, pointing to some sentence.
units.zh: 有那么一瞬，你想趁争论尚未失控、变成拳脚相向之前制止他们。可转念一想，这又不是头一回见两位神职人员吵得激烈，他们本就如此。于是，你决定让两人自己谈出个结果。过了一会儿，嗓门渐渐低下，两颗脑袋也一同凑到书前。他们安静翻阅，顺着字行看去，不时碰到彼此的头。最后，{#1}修士甲{/#1}抬起身，指着一句话。

units.source: Now, this isn't the first time you've seen two monks squabbling. The last time it happened the debaters hashed it out right quick. So naturally you think these two will do the same. Alas, it isn't to be. Their voices grow louder and louder. You never knew monks could be so sharp-tongued. Fierceness and lewdness don't even begin to describe the insults being thrown back and forth. It isn't but a few seconds later that they are on the ground, wrestling and punching until you order {#1}Otherguy{/#1} to put an end to it.
units.zh: 你并非头一回见到修士争吵。上一次，那些辩论者很快便谈妥了，所以你自然以为这两位也会如此。可惜，事情并未如你所料。他们嗓门越来越高，你从不知道修士的嘴竟能这么毒。凶狠、下流都不足以形容那些来回对骂的污言秽语。没过几秒，两人便滚到地上，扭打挥拳，直到你命令{#1}另一名弟兄{/#1}把他们拉开。

units.source: {#1}Raider{/#1} is sitting out beside the campfire, his eyes set deep into the flames. A few moments ago, a couple of the men were heard yelling at him. A past as a raider isn't winning the man many friends. The hedge knight, {#2}Hedgeknight{/#2}, walks over and stands there beside him. As the two exchange glances, you're suddenly worried a fight you can't stop is going to break out. Instead, the hedge knight takes a seat. He speaks calmly, though his deep voice is still soundly scary.

He blinks just long enough for the weapon to sheathe itself in his shoulder. He blinks again, just long enough for the pain to start kicking in. Within a moment, {#2}Juggler{/#2} is bowled over, clutching his wound in howling pain. A few men tend to him while others can only laugh.

units.source: The axe {#1}Juggler{/#1} asked for is picked up and heaved toward him. It spins at an awkward angle as if the man who threw it intentionally sent it wobbling in indeterminate ways. Not expecting this, the juggler adjusts to try and catch the haywire axe handle, but the weapon smashes into one of the daggers and cuts across his shoulder. He falls to the ground in an instant, a shower of knives falling all around him. While some men tend to his wounds, other can't help but be delighted in his suffering.
units.zh: 有人拿起{#1}杂耍艺人{/#1}要的斧头，朝他掷去。斧头转得十分别扭，像是出手的人存心让它乱晃。杂耍艺人始料未及，急忙调整姿势，想抓住乱转的斧柄；可斧头撞上一把匕首，划过他的肩膀。他瞬间倒地，刀子如雨落在四周。一些人上前处理伤口，另一些则忍不住幸灾乐祸。

Not expecting this, the juggler adjusts to try and catch the haywire axe handle, but the weapon smashes into one of the daggers and cuts across his shoulder. He falls to the ground in an instant, a shower of knives falling all around him. While some men tend to his wounds, other can't help but be delighted in his suffering.

units.source: {#1}Nonjuggler{/#1} picks up the requested flail and, after a moment's hesitation, lofts it toward {#2}Juggler{/#2}. Mid-flight, the chain of the weapon wraps around the handle. The juggler seems to adjust himself for it, but at the last moment the chain unfurls, whipping back around with deadly intent. You see the man's eyes flare open as he sees a calamity he can't stop from coming. The flail crashes through his maelstrom of metal and clips him in the face. Knocked out cold, he spins on his feet and collapses to the ground. A falling dagger penetrates his leg and the axe cuts tumbles right into his hip. The men gasp in horror and soon every one of them gets up and rushes to his aid.
units.zh: {#1}扔兵器的弟兄{/#1}拿起他要的连枷，迟疑片刻，抛向{#2}杂耍艺人{/#2}。连枷飞到半空，铁链绕住了握柄。艺人似乎已经调整好动作，准备接住，可就在最后一刻，铁链突然展开，凶险地甩了回来。他眼睛猛然睁大，眼看着灾祸逼近，却再也无力阻止。连枷撞穿飞旋的利刃，打在他脸上。他当场昏厥，身子打了个转，倒在地上。一把落下的匕首刺穿了他的腿，斧头也翻滚着砍进了他的胯部。弟兄们惊恐地倒吸一口凉气，随即纷纷起身，冲上去救人。

units.source: You sit down and let the men throw {#1}Juggler{/#1} a few knives and daggers. They come in and at all shapes and sizes, and from all angles, but he catches them with ease and starts tossing them up into the air, their revolutions glinting and sparkling in the sunlight. Being that each weapon carries a different weight, you're impressed by how able he is to keep them all going in seamless unison.

units.source: A flail is retrieved and lobbed toward {#1}Juggler{/#1}. Everyone grimaces as the flail snakes and twirls and undulates toward the spinning storm of weaponry the juggler calls his 'act.' But, just like the axe, it is quickly absorbed into the maelstrom of metal. Louder than ever, the men get to their feet to cheer and clap. A few sigh in relief, wiping sweat from their brow, while others can only grin and clap, being rather disappointed that nothing spectacularly awful didn't happen, but impressed nonetheless.

units.source: You find {#1}Swordmaster{/#1} struggling to set himself down on a tree stump. As he gingerly lowers, you see his legs quaking as though they can barely bend at all. He lets out a long sigh after he takes his seat. His sword is beside him. It is younger than the hands that own it, a replacement of a replacement of a replacement. He shows no fondness for it, but when he touches it you sense there is a reflection in the very idea of a sword, of how a man lengthens himself with it, and how he shortens others by its very blade. You turn to leave, hoping to give the swordmaster time to himself, but he notices your departure and calls out.
units.zh: 你看见{#1}剑术大师{/#1}正费力地往一截树桩上坐。他小心翼翼地压低身子，双腿直打颤，仿佛根本弯不下去。终于坐稳，他长长地叹了口气。剑放在身旁，比握它的那双手年轻得多，是换过一把又一把之后留下的。他对这把剑并无多少眷恋，可手指碰到剑身时，你仍能觉出他对“剑”本身的感慨：人借它延伸自己的臂膀，也借它斩短别人的性命。你转身想走，留他独处一会儿，他却察觉了你的动静，出声叫住你。

units.source: While you expect the men you hire to leave their old lives behind, sometimes it is not so. It appears that {#1}Caravanhand{/#1} and {#2}Raider{/#2} are well acquainted: the caravan hand once dealt with the raider personally in some sort of battle that ended with no victors. Now they seek to finish what they'd started long ago, the two tumbling about on the ground, throwing punches and elbows and some spit if an eye or cheek calls for it. You separate the two yourself, pulling them apart and making it quite clear that they are sellswords now, not enemies. You force the two to shake hands and they do so. The caravan hand nods.
units.zh: 你指望招来的弟兄能把过去抛在身后，可有时偏偏做不到。{#1}当过商队杂工的弟兄{/#1}与{#2}劫掠者{/#2}显然早就认识：商队杂工曾在一场没分出胜负的交锋中，亲手与这位劫掠者过过招。如今，两人打算把旧账算完。他们在地上翻滚，拳头、肘子轮番招呼，瞅见眼睛和脸颊，也不忘啐上一口。你亲自把他们拽开，说得再明白不过：现在你们是一起拿钱打仗的弟兄，不再是仇敌。你逼两人握手，他们照办了。商队杂工点点头。

units.zh: "凡人，我将赐你死亡。你将安卧于它的慰藉之中，而死亡将降临你的敌人。{#1}被选作祭品的弟兄{/#1}不会消逝，他将永远与你同在，这是我的承诺。"

units.source: A whiteness snaps back over you, a rush of wind, tent flaps curling outward, candleflames tilting impossibly without going out, and a frigid coolness that has your first breath seen floating across the air. {#1}Cultist{/#1} is nowhere to be seen. You quickly get up and touch your face and skin, making sure that you are all that you're supposed to be. The vision remains, though, and its pulsing imprint has left behind a grisly reality that what the cultist has suggested is something to be measured seriously.
units.zh: 一片白光骤然将你拉回。狂风涌动，帐帘向外卷起，烛火以不可思议的角度倾斜，却没有熄灭。刺骨的寒意中，你呼出的第一口气化作白雾，飘过眼前。{#1}邪教徒{/#1}已不知所踪。你急忙起身，摸过自己的脸和皮肤，确认自己仍是原来的自己。可那幻象仍挥之不去，烙印般在脑中跳动，留下一个可怕的事实：教徒提出的建议，你不得不认真权衡。

units.source: You decide to fall to the undeniable impression that Davkul would be most unhappy with your failure to obey. But {#1}Sacrifice{/#1} also has earned a departing word from you. Clearing up your face, you step out of your tent and go to speak to the man. Perhaps just hearing his voice will knock some sense into you before you step off the ledge into an insane void from which this act has no doubt been beckoned.
units.zh: 有一点已不容否认：若你拒不服从，达夫库尔将极为不悦。你决定屈从。可{#1}被选作祭品的弟兄{/#1}也值得你亲口道别。你整了整神色，走出帐篷，去找他说话。也许，只要听见他的声音，你就能清醒过来，不至于踏入那疯狂的深渊——这般行径，无疑正是从那里受到的召唤。

units.source: You reach over to the blanket and draw it back. You jump to your feet and nearly knock the whole tent over. In the bed is not {#1}Sacrifice{/#1}, but a torso, its flesh torn asunder and stretched around armor made of unknown metal, teeth for rivets, tendons for strappings, bones for pauldrons, a cuirass of absolute carnage. {#2}Cultist{/#2} stands in the tent's opening.
units.zh: 你伸手掀开毯子，随即猛地跳起，险些掀翻整顶帐篷。床上躺着的并非{#1}被选作祭品的弟兄{/#1}，而是一截躯干：血肉被撕开、撑展，包裹着某种未知金属铸成的盔甲。牙齿做铆钉，肌腱做束带，骨头做肩甲，整副胸甲就是一场血腥屠戮的凝结。{#2}邪教徒{/#2}站在帐篷入口。

In the bed is not %sacrifice%, but a torso, its flesh torn asunder and stretched around armor made of unknown metal, teeth for rivets, tendons for strappings, bones for pauldrons, a cuirass of absolute carnage. %cultist% stands in the tent's opening.

units.source: This... this is not what you were expecting. You don't even know what you were expecting, but this could never have been imagined or prepared for. What's done is done, and may the soul of {#1}Sacrifice{/#1} rest in peace. It is unlikely you ever will.
units.zh: 这……这不是你预想的结果。你甚至不知道自己原先在期待什么，但眼前这一幕，绝无可能事先想象，更无从准备。事已至此，但愿{#1}被选作祭品的弟兄{/#1}的灵魂能安息。你恐怕永远也不能了。

units.source: Despite the horror which you have just been witness to, you decide that {#1}Sacrifice{/#1} shall live. Just as you stand to go tell {#2}Cultist{/#2} of this, half the candles in the room suddenly blow out. Tendrils of smoke waft upward, a twisting haze through which, for but a moment, you swear you see a hard edged and angry visage turn and fade away. You get the feeling that {#3}Cultist{/#3} already knows what choice you've made. You stay in the tent and light those candles back up.
units.zh: 尽管刚刚目睹了那般恐怖的景象，你仍决定让{#1}被选作祭品的弟兄{/#1}活下去。你正起身去告诉{#2}邪教徒{/#2}，屋内半数蜡烛忽然熄灭。缕缕烟雾升起，在扭曲的薄霭中，有那么一瞬，你确信看见一张棱角分明、怒气冲冲的面孔转身消散。你隐隐觉得，{#3}邪教徒{/#3}已经知道了你的选择。于是你留在帐篷里，把蜡烛一一重新点亮。

units.source: Word is spreading about {#1}Eunuch{/#1} the eunuch. Apparently, him and some brothers visited the town brothel. The whores and brothers alike initially made fun of the eunuch, but he demanded only five minutes with the most experienced of the ladies. She came back out after two minutes and the rumors about {#2}Eunuch{/#2}'s bedroom prowess has only exploded from there.
units.zh: 关于{#1}阉人{/#1}的传闻渐渐传开。据说，他跟几个弟兄去了镇上的妓院。起初，妓女和弟兄们都拿他取笑，他却只要求与最有经验的女子独处五分钟。才过两分钟，那女子就出来了，从此，关于{#2}阉人{/#2}房中本事的传闻便越传越盛。

units.source: Now, half the town, more precisely its women, speak highly of the {#1}Companyname{/#1} and would love to see it visit again. {#2}Eunuch{/#2} himself gives you a wink and a smile. You notice that he's rather warty around the lips.
units.zh: 如今，半个镇子——更准确地说，是镇上的女人们——都对{#1}〈战团名〉{/#1}赞不绝口，巴不得战团再来。{#2}阉人{/#2}本人笑着朝你眨了眨眼。你注意到，他嘴边长着不少疣。

units.source: You find {#1}Farmhand{/#1} and {#2}Butcher{/#2} arguing with one another over a piece of meat. The farmhand raises his voice.
units.zh: 你发现{#1}农场帮工{/#1}和{#2}屠夫{/#2}正为一块肉争得不可开交。农场帮工提高嗓门。

provenance.method: Independently reviewed exact game variable template

units.source: {#1}Fisherman{/#1}, the ol' fisherman, regals the company with tales of his fishing days.
units.zh: 上了年纪的{#1}渔夫{/#1}向弟兄们讲起往昔捕鱼的故事，逗得众人兴致盎然。

units.source: {#1}Otherguy{/#1} approaches with a pained look on his face. His helmet is in hand as he wipes his brow.
units.zh: {#1}另一名弟兄{/#1}神情难受地走来，一手拿着头盔，一手抹额头。

units.source: You get up and have him lead you to whatever it is that's causing an issue. You come across a throng of brothers circled around something or someone. Breaking your way through the crowd, the company quiets as you come into the clearing to find {#1}Flagellant{/#1} the flagellant unconscious on the ground.
units.zh: 你站起身，让他带你去看看究竟出了什么事。一群弟兄围在那里，不知围着的是人还是东西。你挤进人群，众人随之安静下来。空地上，{#1}苦修者{/#1}已经昏死过去。

units.source: {#1}Flagellant{/#1} the flagellant is found sitting cross-legged before a campfire. He's all alone save the millmoths fluttering dangerously close to the flames. Sensing your presence, he calls you over. You take a seat beside him and he smiles at you.
units.zh: 你发现{#1}苦修者{/#1}独自盘腿坐在营火前，只有几只飞蛾在火焰边危险地扑腾着。察觉到你来了，他招呼你过去。你在他身旁坐下，他朝你微微一笑。

units.source: Suddenly, {#1}Graverobber{/#1} the graverobber appears by your side, his smell skewering your thoughts with miasmic proficiency. He's hardly a man at all, but a golem, mudslaked and grass-peppered with two white eyes peering out. Sighing, you ask what he wants. He thumbs over one shoulder, the other occupied by a shovel.
units.zh: 突然，{#1}盗墓贼{/#1}出现在你身旁，他身上的恶臭像瘴气利箭，一下刺穿了你的思绪。他几乎已不像个人，倒像一具泥塑的魔像，浑身糊满烂泥，撒着草屑，只有两只眼睛露出白光。你叹了口气，问他要什么。他一边肩上扛着铲子，另一只手的拇指朝身后一指。
