units.source: {#1}Graverobber{/#1} brings you to a big hole in the ground. The top half of a skeleton is at the bottom, its arms loose over the earth as though it had bedded there for a night's rest. Empty eye sockets look up at you. The graverobber crouches and grabs something. He wipes the mud and worms off it and hands it over.
units.zh: {#1}盗墓贼{/#1}把你带到一个大坑旁。坑底露着半具骷髅，双臂松松搭在土上，像是躺在那里歇了一宿；空洞的眼窝正对着你。盗墓贼蹲下，拿起一件东西，擦去泥土与虫子，递过来。

units.source: While looking down at the goods, {#1}Historian{/#1} the rather astute scholar and historian sidles up next to you. He's rubbing his chin and a faint hum ruminates deeply within him.
units.zh: 你低头打量物件时，颇为敏锐的{#1}历史学者{/#1}挪到身旁，摸着下巴，喉间发出沉思的低吟。

units.source: You turn to him to ask what he's going on about. He snaps his fingers and points down at what the graverobber had found. He explains that this isn't just any chest plate or weapon, but indeed the gear of a famous fighter, nobleman, and womanizer, {#1}Noblename{/#1}.
units.zh: 你转头问他在念叨什么。他打了个响指，指向盗墓贼的收获，解释这不是寻常胸甲或武器，而是{#1}〈贵族姓名〉{/#1}的装备——那人既是著名战士与贵族，也是个风流浪子。

units.source: {#1}Graverobber{/#1} the grimy graverobber enters your tent with his hands behind his back. You don't wish to delay what madness has been brought before you much longer, so you go ahead and ask what the man wants.
units.zh: 脏兮兮的{#1}盗墓贼{/#1}背着双手走进帐篷。你不愿再等他慢吞吞地说出这回又有什么疯主意，索性直接问他想干什么。

units.source: Having excused yourself from the excavating expedition, you get back to work. Time flies, millmoths arcing in rote loops about a candle that droops lower and lower, its glassy flame so easily flicked to the wingbeats of the creatures about it. Finally, {#1}Graverobber{/#1} returns, heaving a bit of a chest into the tent. He looks more mud than man.
units.zh: 你婉拒了同行挖坟，继续处理自己的事。时辰飞逝，飞蛾绕着蜡烛反复盘旋，烛身越来越短，明亮的火苗随着翅膀扇动轻轻摇曳。终于，{#1}盗墓贼{/#1}回来了，费力将一只箱子拖进帐篷。他浑身泥浆，几乎看不出人样。

Finally, %graverobber% returns, heaving a bit of a chest into the tent. He looks more mud than man.

units.source: Having excused yourself from the excavating expedition, you get back to work. Time flies, millmoths arcing in rote loops about a candle that droops lower and lower, its glassy flame so easily flicked to the wingbeats of the creatures about it. Finally, {#1}Graverobber{/#1} returns, the first sign of him the edge of your tent flap moving just so. You set your quillpen down and ask the man to enter. He does so, rather tentatively, as a man about to cross a threshold he'd rather not. Even in the dim candlelight you can see the colors darkness is so ordinarily good at hiding: purples and blues and dark reds. He grins sheepishly.
units.zh: 你谢绝了这趟挖坟的邀约，回去继续办事。时间飞逝，飞蛾绕着蜡烛一圈圈打转，烛身越烧越短，晶亮的火苗随着周围振翅的微风轻轻摇晃。终于，{#1}盗墓贼{/#1}回来了。帐篷门帘的边角微微一动，最先透露了他的到来。你放下羽毛笔，叫他进来。他犹犹豫豫地迈过门槛，仿佛实在不愿踏进这里。即便烛光昏暗，你仍看清了那些平时能被黑夜掩去的颜色：青一块、紫一块，还有暗红的血迹。他难为情地咧嘴笑了笑。

units.source: {#1}Townname{/#1} is not the pillar upon which you wish to sacrifice your good standing in the world - or at least, what good standing a mercenary can have. You tell {#2}Graverobber{/#2} that not only will you not be accompanying him, but that you refuse to let him go off and do this alone. He pouts like a young hunter whose bow has been taken away by an angry father.
units.zh: 你不想为了{#1}〈城镇名〉{/#1}这点事，葬送自己在世上的好名声——至少是佣兵还能拥有的那点名声。你告诉{#2}盗墓贼{/#2}，不但不会陪他去，也不许他独自行动。他撅起嘴，活像一个被愤怒父亲没收了弓的小猎人。

units.source: You and {#1}Graverobber{/#1} stalk low through the bushes, a gangly duo of absurdity, silhouettes murky and ruminating of obvious hijinks even in the darkest of nights. The two of you enter the graveyard as though you were to happen about it by accident, merrily pretending that what is to unfold next would surely not come from two stranges such as yourselves.
units.zh: 你和{#1}盗墓贼{/#1}弓着身子，在灌木间潜行。这两个瘦高家伙凑成的荒唐搭档，即便在最漆黑的夜里，那两道模糊轮廓也透着明摆着要干坏事的鬼祟。你们装作偶然路过，走进墓园，煞有介事地假装接下来要发生的事，绝不会与自己这两个陌生人有关。

provenance.method: Independently reviewed exact game variable template

units.source: With a swift crack of your spade, the gothic gate is broken open. The twang of metal on metal is sent grumbling between the gravestones and swaying tree branches seem to snicker at your rather loud trespass. When you swing the gate open, the hinges squall as if they themselves were awakened spirits. You enter the little square plot and lean against the spires of the fence. A short order gets {#1}Graverobber{/#1} to work while you keep a look out like a man unimpressed by the nature of his own crimes. Some minutes of scrupulous shoveling later and the robber of graves is finished. What ends up being found is a very large coffin that has no hopes of being dragged out of the ground, not with just two men anyway.
units.zh: 你挥铲猛地一砸，撬开那扇尖拱铁门。金属相撞的嗡鸣在墓碑间低低回荡，摇曳的树枝仿佛也在窃笑，讥讽你这场动静过大的擅闯。你推开门，铰链尖叫起来，像是它们自己成了被惊醒的亡魂。你走进这块方正的小墓地，倚着围栏尖顶，简短地吩咐{#1}盗墓贼{/#1}动手，自己则负责望风，对亲手犯下的罪行颇不以为意。几分钟仔细挖掘后，盗墓贼干完了活。下面露出一口极大的棺材，根本别想拖出土坑，至少只靠两个人不行。

units.source: Using the same manner with which you dealt the gate a blow, you break the latches off the casket and throw it open. A freshly-dead man stares back up at you, two stones painted with eyes rolling away from his sockets. The sight startles you, but you quickly start rifling through the dead man's baggage. As it turns out, {#1}Graverobber{/#1} was right: the man was buried with great satchels of gold and goblets and golden goblets. You take it all, close the casket, and sneak back out of the graveyard.
units.zh: 你用刚才对付铁门的办法，砸断棺材上的扣锁，掀开棺盖。一个刚死不久的男人仰面望着你，两颗画着眼睛的石头从眼窝上滚落。这景象让你一惊，但你很快便翻起死者的随葬物。事实证明，{#1}盗墓贼{/#1}说得没错：陪他下葬的，有整袋整袋的金子，有高脚杯，还有金高脚杯。你们全都收走，合上棺材，悄悄溜出了墓园。

A freshly-dead man stares back up at you, two stones painted with eyes rolling away from his sockets. The sight startles you, but you quickly start rifling through the dead man's baggage. As it turns out, %graverobber% was right: the man was buried with great satchels of gold and goblets and golden goblets. You take it all, close the casket, and sneak back out of the graveyard.

units.source: You enter the mausoleum like a man fearful that the door behind him might forever snap closed. The coffin rests on a slab of marble with candles burning about its four corners. While there was no wind outside, you can't help but hear a faint moan of it circling about the room. Shaking away your fears, you and {#1}Graverobber{/#1} push the casket's lid off, careful not to let it drop off the otherside and presumably wake half the town.
units.zh: 你走进陵墓，心里直犯嘀咕，生怕身后的门突然合上，再也打不开。棺椁放在大理石台上，四角点着蜡烛。外面明明无风，墓室里却仿佛有微弱的风声盘旋呜咽。你甩开惧意，与{#1}盗墓贼{/#1}一起推开棺盖，小心不让它从另一侧滑落，否则怕是半个镇子都会被惊醒。

The coffin rests on a slab of marble with candles burning about its four corners. While there was no wind outside, you can't help but hear a faint moan of it circling about the room. Shaking away your fears, you and %graverobber% push the casket's lid off, careful not to let it drop off the otherside and presumably wake half the town.

units.source: Inside the sarcophagus, you find a man attired in a knight's clothing: a helmet, chest plate, and shield. His sword crosses his body from neck to groin, his hands clasped around the handle in a battle-ready embrace. You look to {#1}Graverobber{/#1} who shrugs.
units.zh: 石棺里躺着一人，穿戴着骑士的行头：头盔、胸甲，还有盾牌。一把剑平放在他身上，从颈部一直伸到胯下，双手紧握剑柄，仿佛随时准备迎战。你看向{#1}盗墓贼{/#1}，他耸耸肩。

units.source: Seeing as how you don't plan to leave empty handed, you nod again. The dead knight puts up quite the fight as {#1}Graverobber{/#1} struggles to free him of that which he no longer needs. After a few minutes of battle, you lend a hand in removing the helmet. What falls out is a great bundle of blonde hair. {#2}Graverobber{/#2} steps back.
units.zh: 你可不打算空手而归，于是又点了点头。要剥下这些死者已不再需要的东西，却颇费周折，{#1}盗墓贼{/#1}简直像在跟死骑士搏斗。折腾几分钟后，你也搭手帮忙摘下头盔。一大蓬金发随之散落。{#2}盗墓贼{/#2}后退一步。

units.source: You grab {#1}Graverobber{/#1} by the collar and tell him to leave. There's no sense in causing trouble. The watchman barks at you as you depart.
units.zh: 你揪住{#1}盗墓贼{/#1}的衣领，叫他走人。没必要惹麻烦。你们离开时，守夜人仍在身后吼叫。

units.source: After burying a dead comrade, {#1}Gravedigger{/#1} pitches his shovel into the earth and grabs {#2}Graverobber{/#2} by his tunic, driving him backward as he lifts him into the air. Before even a word or threat can be exchanged, the dangling man throws a kick into his attacker's groin. They both fall to the ground and immediately start tumbling about in the mud. The muck makes them indistinguishable, but their fit of anger is well heard.
units.zh: 刚埋葬一位死去的战友，{#1}掘墓人{/#1}便把铁锹往地上一插，一把揪住{#2}盗墓贼{/#2}的衣襟，将他提离地面，朝后推去。还没来得及争吵或放出狠话，双脚悬空的家伙便一脚踹中对方裤裆。两人一同倒地，立即在泥里扭打起来。泥浆糊得谁也认不出谁，可怒骂声听得一清二楚。

units.source: {#1}Killerontherun{/#1} is being held down by one brother's knee, while {#2}Otherguy1{/#2} and {#3}Otherguy2{/#3} look about ready to chop his head off. Seeing your arrival, the men calm down for a moment. They explain that the killer tried to slay one of them. Indeed, the brother has a nick on his neck. A little bit deeper and something other than words would be coming out of his mouth right about now. The men demand {#4}Killerontherun{/#4} be hanged for this attempted murder.
units.zh: 一个弟兄用膝盖把{#1}在逃杀人犯{/#1}死死压在地上，{#2}弟兄甲{/#2}和{#3}弟兄乙{/#3}则像是随时准备砍下他的脑袋。见你来了，众人暂时冷静了一些，解释说这杀人犯刚才想杀掉他们中的一个。那弟兄脖子上果然有一道伤口，再深一点，此刻从他嘴里出来的恐怕就不只是话了。众人要求把{#4}在逃杀人犯{/#4}绞死，惩罚这次谋杀未遂。

units.source: You order the man flogged. {#1}Killerontherun{/#1} spits on your name as the brothers tie him up to a tree. You say do that again and you'll add more lashings. They rip his shirt off and take turns with the whip as you stand by the side, counting. On the first lash a straight line of skin is stripped from his back. The man flinches and you hear the ropes that bind him draw taut as his hands clench into fists. By the fifth lashing he is no longer standing. By the tenth he is no longer awake. After five more you call it and order the men to take him down and tend his wounds.
units.zh: 你命人鞭笞。弟兄们将{#1}在逃杀人犯{/#1}绑上树时，他破口辱骂你。你说，再骂就多加几鞭。他们撕开他的上衣，轮流执鞭，你在旁边数着。第一鞭便从背上抽掉一长条皮。那人猛地一缩，双手攥拳，你听见捆他的绳索骤然绷紧。到第五鞭，他已经站不住了。第十鞭时，他已失去知觉。又打了五鞭，你才叫停，命弟兄们把他放下来，照料伤口。

units.source: You order the man hanged. Half the company cheers and {#1}Killerontherun{/#1} screams a shriek rather suitable for seeing death ordered to his side. They drag the man beneath a tree. Ropes are thrown up over the branches, again and again, looping and drawing taut. One man ties a noose while the others cheer and clap and drink beer. A stool is placed and the condemned man is forced to stand on it. As {#2}Killerontherun{/#2}'s head is put into the noose, he says he has a word for all of you, but whatever he has to say is cut off when {#3}Otherguy1{/#3} kicks the stool out from beneath him.
units.zh: 你下令将他吊死。半个战团欢呼起来，{#1}在逃杀人犯{/#1}则发出凄厉的尖叫，倒很符合一个刚听见自己死刑判决的人。他们把他拖到树下，一遍遍将绳子抛过树枝，绕好，拉紧。一人打着绞索，其他人则欢呼、鼓掌、喝酒。凳子摆好，受刑者被强迫站上去。{#2}在逃杀人犯{/#2}的脑袋套进绞索时，他说还有话要对你们所有人讲，可话还没出口，{#3}弟兄甲{/#3}便踢飞了他脚下的凳子。

units.source: This is not a good way to die. It is by an executioner's hand or means. Ordinarily a man dropped from a platform breaks his neck, or is even decapitated. This man hangs choking and kicking. You hear some screams in his lungs, but they struggle to get past his throat. A few minutes pass and he is still fighting. {#1}Otherguy2{/#1} steps over to the dying man, grabbing one of his jerking feet to keep him still, and with his free hand he stabs {#2}Killerontherun{/#2} in the heart. And that was that.
units.zh: 这死法很不好受。刽子手的手段通常利落得多：人从高台坠下，不是折断脖子，便是连脑袋也被扯掉。而他却吊在那里，窒息着，踢蹬着。你能听见肺里挤出的惨叫，却很难穿过喉咙。几分钟过去，他仍在挣扎。{#1}弟兄乙{/#1}走到垂死之人身边，抓住一只抽动的脚，将他稳住，另一只手拔刀刺进{#2}在逃杀人犯{/#2}的心脏。至此，一切结束。

units.source: Well, {#1}Killerontherun{/#1} isn't dead, but he stands before you broken and beaten. It looks like vengeful justice found him out anyway. He demands that some suspected brothers be punished for going around your orders. You consider this, but then ask the man what will happen if you continue this cycle of violence. It's hard to see the man's face as it is puffed up in blacks and purples, and his eyes are lost behind puckered lids, but he nods gingerly. You are right, he says. It is best to let this whole thing die down lest it get out of control.
units.zh: {#1}在逃杀人犯{/#1}倒是没死，可站在你面前时，已经被打得不成人形。看来，报复终究找上了他。他要求惩罚几个涉嫌违抗你命令的弟兄。你想了想，反问他：若继续这般以暴还暴，最后会怎样？他满脸青紫肿胀，眼睛埋在鼓起的眼皮后，几乎看不清神情，只小心地点头。他说，你是对的。最好让整件事慢慢平息，免得彻底失控。

units.source: You see that the bannerman is carrying a sigil of {#1}Noblehouse{/#1}. Behind him another horseman is dragging a travois with a few shackled men for cargo. When the men arrive, their leader stands up between the withers of his horse and points at you before talking.
units.zh: 你看见掌旗手举着{#1}〈贵族家族名〉{/#1}的纹章。后方另一名骑手拖着一副曳架，上面载着几个戴镣铐的人。众人来到面前，领头者从马鞍上撑起身，指向你，开口说道。

units.source: "Mercenary! We have by the lord's authority the right to claim the - shackled! - hands of a sir {#1}Criminal{/#1}. Said man is within your midst. He must pay for his crimes. Hand him over immediately and you will be rewarded."
units.zh: "佣兵！奉领主之命，我们有权将{#1}被通缉者{/#1}这位先生拿下——戴上镣铐！此人就在你们之中，必须为罪行付出代价。立即交人，你会得到奖赏。"

units.source: You stand no chance against these men. Although it pains you mightily, you hand {#1}Criminal{/#1} over. He barks curses at you as the lawmen chain him up, and swears your name into the mud as they throw him in with the rest of the bound men. The captain of the lawmen trots his horse over to you. He sneers at you before throwing a purse of coins to the ground. His body is close and there's an opening in his armor. You could fit a knife in there, right between the ribs, lead the blade right to his heart. It'd be quick. But you wouldn't last much long after, and all of your men would be quickly slain.
units.zh: 你们根本不是这些人的对手。尽管心里难受至极，你还是交出了{#1}被通缉者{/#1}。执法队给他套上锁链时，他冲你破口大骂；被扔进其他捆绑的囚犯堆里时，他仍在诅咒你的名字。队长骑马小跑到你面前，先冷笑一声，再把一袋钱扔在地上。他离得很近，甲胄间露着一条缝。你完全可以从那儿捅进一把刀，穿过肋骨，直刺心脏。很快就能了结。可之后你也活不了多久，手下的弟兄更会被迅速杀光。

units.source: {#1}Randombrother{/#1} plucks one man from his saddle while another brother drives a spear into a horse's chest, bringing both beast and man crashing to the ground. The captain falls off his horse when it rears up in wild fear. It's a hard tumble, but he manages to roll back to his feet only for the bucking horse to clip him in the head. It is a quick, blunt demise that leaves the captain face down in the cradle of his own helmet.
units.zh: {#1}某位弟兄{/#1}将一人从马鞍上拽下，另一个弟兄则把长矛刺进马胸，连人带马一同摔倒。队长的坐骑受惊直立，他也跌下马背。虽摔得重，他还是翻身站了起来，却被乱蹬的马蹄击中头部。他死得突然而干脆，脸朝下栽倒，脑袋埋在自己的头盔里。

units.source: The captain of the lawmen snaps his fingers at one of the bannermen. He hands over a scroll which the captain unfurls before handing it to you. The man you see looks remarkably like {#1}Criminal{/#1}, but since you've been on the road the mercenary has gained a few scars that separate his visage from the one on the paper. But they won't buy that. So you lie instead.
units.zh: 执法队长朝一个掌旗手打了个响指。对方递来一卷纸，队长展开后交到你手里。画上的人与{#1}被通缉者{/#1}像极了，只是这一路上，佣兵脸上添了几道疤，与画像稍有不同。可凭这点糊弄不过去。于是，你撒了个谎。

units.source: "The man you're looking for is dead. He was a criminal, just as you said, and we found him thieving from our foods. {#1}Otherbro{/#1} ran a sword through him when we'd found out."
units.zh: "你们要找的人已经死了。他确实是个罪犯，正如你所说。我们发现他偷吃粮食，{#1}另一位弟兄{/#1}一剑捅穿了他。"

units.source: "We've no time for this. What I have here is 1000 crowns. Take it and go away. Stay, and earn yourself a grave. Your choice, lawman."

units.source: You walk directly toward the captain, stopping halfway between your men and his. With your fists to your hips, you call out to the captain's lawmen, asking if they know the name of the {#1}Companyname{/#1}. You see a few of the riders shift up on their saddles, balancing tented arms on their pommels as they stare intently at your banner. They quickly sit back down and hushed whispers trickle down and back up their battle line.

units.source: One man calls out, asking if it's true that you shorn the noses of those you slay. It is not true, but you've no reason to spill the truth. Another man asks if {#1}Randombrother{/#1} is in your ranks, and if he has a necklace of ears and eats bonemeal for breakfast. You stifle the urge to laugh, only nodding in return. Quite naturally, the rumors overtake your opponents and they begin to cry out that this fight is not theirs to have.
units.zh: 有人喊着问，你是否真的会割下所杀之人的鼻子。这不是真的，但你没理由道出实情。另一个人问，{#1}某位弟兄{/#1}是否在你麾下，是不是真的戴着耳朵串成的项链，早饭吃骨粉。你强忍笑意，只是点头。流言很快淹没了对面的队伍，他们开始嚷嚷，说这仗根本不该由自己来打。

Quite naturally, the rumors overtake your opponents and they begin to cry out that this fight is not theirs to have.

units.source: The company marches into the mountains, or what {#1}Randombrother{/#1} poetically referred to as the 'realm's tits'. Clouds start passing at eye-level and the air gets so thin it's like you're breathing through a straw. Snow crunches underfoot and harsh winds threaten to your eyes into ice cubes. Despite the steep escarpments and dangerous crevasses to cross, {#2}Miner{/#2} the miner seems rather happy to be this far up.
units.zh: 战团向群山进发，或者用{#1}某位弟兄{/#1}那颇有诗意的说法，正攀上“王国的奶子”。云从眼前飘过，空气稀薄得仿佛只能隔着麦秆吸气。脚下积雪咯吱作响，凛冽寒风几乎要把眼珠冻成冰块。尽管一路得翻越陡崖、跨过险峻裂隙，{#2}矿工{/#2}却因能爬到这么高而兴奋不已。

units.source: The man raises a leg, it goes into an angle no man's leg should before planting back on the ground. He twirls, arms above his head. He then fans his arms out as if to fly. It's actually quite beautiful, though you'd never admit as much to any living soul. You watch as the minstrel continues, leaning forward when suddenly he rips a horrendous fart right into {#1}Otherbrother{/#1}'s face.
units.zh: 他抬起一条腿，弯出常人不该有的角度，才重新落地。接着举臂过头，旋转身体，再把双臂展开，仿佛要飞。其实相当优美，不过你绝不会向任何活人承认。你看着吟游诗人继续表演，身体向前一倾，忽然对着{#1}一名弟兄{/#1}的脸，放了一个骇人的响屁。

units.source: With rations down to nothing, {#1}Ratcatcher{/#1} feebly enters your tent, the moans of some hungry men passing by before the flaps close behind him. He explains that he has a resolution to your food problem. You fear to ask what it is, but you've little choice now. The ratchatcher swings a burlap sack onto the table. Some shape of it moves, skittering and bobbing and squealing. The man smashes it with his fist before smiling at you.
units.zh: 口粮已经耗尽，{#1}捕鼠人{/#1}有气无力地走进你的帐篷。帐帘合上之前，外头还传来几个饥饿弟兄的哀叹。他说自己有办法解决粮食问题。你有点不敢问是什么，可眼下也没得选。捕鼠人把一只粗麻袋甩到桌上，里头有什么东西乱窜乱拱，吱吱尖叫。他一拳砸下去，随后冲你笑了笑。

units.source: You come across {#1}Ratcatcher{/#1} sitting with his hands full of rope. He's got the cords looping so ferociously - as ropes can be looped - that you worry to not put your foot close to it. Curious, you ask the man what he's up to. As though he were expecting just that question, he quickly raises his project into the air and announces he's fashioned himself a net. Ah! You put your hands to your hips.
units.zh: 你撞见{#1}捕鼠人{/#1}坐着，满手都是绳子。他打绳圈的劲头凶猛得很——若编绳也称得上凶猛的话——弄得你都不敢把脚靠近。你好奇地问他在忙什么。他仿佛就等这句话，立刻举起手里的活计，宣布自己编好了一张网。啊哈！你双手叉腰。

units.source: You turn around, crossing your arms and jacking a boot against a crate. Staring out across the land, you tell {#1}Sellsword{/#1} that the company has been through a lot together and everyone, yourself especially, would hate to see him go. He has a second family here with the the {#2}Companyname{/#2} and that's a rare treat in the mercenary world. Where he's going there is no guarantee of what he may find. You know, because you've been there. You've been in his very shoes, and you took those shoes and walked. And regretted it.
units.zh: 你转过身，抱起双臂，将一只靴子抵在箱上，望向远处大地。你告诉{#1}佣兵{/#1}，战团一同熬过这么多事，谁也不愿看他离开，尤其是你。他在{#2}〈战团名〉{/#2}已经有了第二个家，这在佣兵行当里何其难得。到了别处会遇上什么，却没人能保证。你知道，因为你也曾面临同样的抉择。当时你一走了之，后来却后悔了。

units.source: "I'm the one in charge here! Me! Who has the money? Me! If it weren't for me, none of y'all would even be here! You'd still be in the pits of whatever old lives you had! You should be groveling before my feet for the opportunities I have provided! And {#1}Cocky{/#1}, if you contest me again I swear to the gods I will have you flogged and hanged, understand?"
units.zh: "这里我说了算！是我！谁掏的钱？我！没有我，你们能在这儿？你们还在从前那摊烂泥里打滚呢！我给你们活路，你们就该趴在我脚边道谢！还有你，{#1}自负的弟兄{/#1}，再敢跟我叫板，我向诸神发誓，先抽你鞭子，再把你吊死，听懂了吗？"

units.source: The outburst instantly quiets the camp. {#1}Cocky{/#1} nods and backs away. A few of the men murmur between themselves as you take your seat again.
units.zh: 这一通怒喝，瞬间让营地鸦雀无声。{#1}自负的弟兄{/#1}点点头，退了下去。你重新落座时，几个弟兄开始低声嘀咕。

units.source: You are beginning to worry that a sort of malaise has fallen upon the men. They sit about the campfire, mindlessly poking sticks into the flames. Each face shows a loss of control, a loss of governance over one's own destiny. If a man can't know if tomorrow will be better than today, then how is he to keep pushing forward? Just as you are about to address this, {#1}Determined{/#1} stands up and so despondent is the mood that even the swift motion by itself catches the company's attention.
units.zh: 你开始担心，某种萎靡正笼罩弟兄们。他们围坐篝火旁，漫不经心地用棍子拨弄火焰。一张张脸都像是失去了对命运的掌控。若连明天能否比今天好都不知道，又该如何坚持走下去？你正准备说点什么，{#1}坚定的弟兄{/#1}却站了起来。营地里如此消沉，单是这一下利落的动作，就吸引了全团的目光。

units.source: You find {#1}Fainthearted{/#1} leaning back and forth before the campfire. His face is speckled with dried blood and his hands are shaking. A few brothers try and talk to him, but none manage to get through. It appears the fainthearted man has been rattled by the horrors of a recent and brutal battle.
units.zh: 你发现{#1}胆怯的弟兄{/#1}坐在篝火前，身子来回摇晃。脸上斑斑血迹已干，双手仍在颤抖。几个弟兄试着跟他说话，却谁也没能唤回他的神。看来，这个胆小的人被最近那场残酷战斗中的恐怖景象吓坏了。

units.source: "Compensate me. Higher pay starting right now. {#1}Newpay{/#1} crowns a day."
units.zh: "给我应得的报酬。从现在起涨薪，每天{#1}〈新日薪〉{/#1}克朗。"

units.zh: 虽然刚吃了败仗，{#1}乐观的弟兄{/#1}仍觉得{#2}〈战团名〉{/#2}前途光明。

units.source: Swamps are no safe place for a man's travels. Judging by the neverending smog and the way the trees bend, there's little doubt that it's a bubbling domicile for all things demonic. At least that's what the druids of these parts like to say. All you find is a couple of dead horses drowned in the mire and a wagon crushed by the mud which has seeped over its wheels and bed. {#1}Randombrother{/#1} rifles through the remains and manages to recover some items.
units.zh: 沼泽绝非适合赶路的地方。看那终年不散的雾气和扭曲的树木，谁都会觉得，这里简直是各种邪物栖身的冒泡烂泥窝。至少，这一带的德鲁伊总是这么说。你们实际找到的，却只有两匹淹死在泥里的马，以及一辆被泥沼压坏的货车。泥浆漫过车轮，灌进车厢。{#1}某位弟兄{/#1}翻找残骸，抢救出几件东西。

units.zh: {#1}当过屠夫的弟兄{/#1}说道。他走上前，开始分割一匹马的尸体，切下几块肉，用大叶子裹好，又抹上些土和盐，吸去水分，随后递了过来。

units.source: You're sitting in your tent enjoying the peace and quiet which, like some increasable quantity, seemingly has accrued in such a way that each day is more enjoyable than the last. Suddenly, {#1}Combatbro1{/#1} and {#2}Combatbro2{/#2} enter. They demand you have a talk. You oblige, fanning your hands across your table and inviting them to sit. They do and quickly state that it has been a long while since they last saw combat. Taken aback, you quite literally lean back in your chair.
units.zh: 你坐在帐篷里享受难得的清静。这份安逸仿佛也能日积月累，让日子一天比一天舒坦。突然，{#1}弟兄甲{/#1}和{#2}弟兄乙{/#2}走了进来，要求与你谈谈。你摊开双手，示意他们坐下。他们刚坐定便直奔主题：已经很久没打过仗了。你一愣，身子不由向椅背靠去。

units.source: {#1}Noble{/#1} suddenly enters your tent. He's attired in armor and his weapon is at his side. It almost seems as if he dressed up for this occasion, and he does indeed stand upright and proper. You ask what it is he wants, and he speaks with his head held high and his eyes looking straight ahead.
units.zh: {#1}贵族弟兄{/#1}突然走进你的帐篷。他披着盔甲，腰佩武器，仿佛专为这次会面整装而来，站姿也格外挺拔端正。你问他有什么事，他昂着头，目视前方，开口说道。

units.source: "It has come to my attention that {#1}Lowborn{/#1} is paid more than I. While I've no issue with the man personally, I do want to point out that he is a man with no birthright to anything but his own two feet. You can't possibly have a lowborn being paid more than a man of the purple. We noblemen deserve more."
units.zh: "我发现，{#1}平民出身的弟兄{/#1}的薪水竟然比我还高。我对他本人并无成见，但必须指出，他出身卑微，生来除了两条腿，什么也继承不了。您总不能让一个贱民拿得比贵族还多。我们这些出身高贵的人，理应得到更多。"

units.source: You don't necessarily agree with him, but at the same time you can see that denying this request may cause some heretofore unseen problems. With a few dashes of your quill pen across the roster scroll, you assign {#1}Noble{/#1} a higher salary and tell him to expect a heavier purse come next payday. The man finally looks at you and bows from the waist.
units.zh: 你未必认同他的说法，可也看得出，拒绝这个要求可能引来未曾料到的麻烦。你在名册上挥了几笔，给{#1}贵族弟兄{/#1}加了军饷，告诉他下次发钱时，钱袋会更沉些。他终于正眼看你，弯腰鞠躬。

units.source: "{#1}Lowborn{/#1} made it through this world by dragging himself out of the mud. You were born with a silver spoon, but this isn't where you were born now is it? So from today consider your pay effectively lowered. You want the right to a higher salary? Earn it."
units.zh: "{#1}平民出身的弟兄{/#1}是从泥里一步步爬出来，才在这世上挣得位置。你生来就含着银匙，可这里不是你出生的地方，对吧？所以从今天起，你的军饷降了。想拿更多？凭本事挣。"

units.source: {#1}Randombrother{/#1} comes to you with a report of your food stocks. He explains that there's not much to go around and what bread is on hand could be better used to build a house or slay a man. Most of the fruit is soft to the touch, covered in what appears to be grey fur. All that's left otherwise has been thrown into a great stew which the men have aptly named 'crotch broth'. To be frank, it isn't looking good.
units.zh: {#1}某位弟兄{/#1}来向你报告食物储备。吃的已经不多，现有的面包硬得拿来砌房子或砸死人，恐怕比填肚子更合适。水果大多一碰就软，表面长着灰毛。剩下的零碎都扔进一大锅里炖着，弟兄们给它起了个颇贴切的名字：裤裆汤。说实话，情况很不妙。

units.source: You turn around and give a knowing glance at {#1}Someguy1{/#1}. He nods back and nocks an arrow. Before the woman can scream, the brother releases the shot and the old man on the porch stumbles backward into the house, followed by a retinue of screaming children. The rest of your company fans out, unsheathing their swords as they run into the fields. A few farmhands try to fight back, but your well-armed band makes short work of them. {#2}Someguy2{/#2} sprints into the homestead and inside you hear a number of cries that, one by one, disappear until there is silence. You hand the woman off to a few brothers, telling them to just make sure she is dead before you leave. A few other sellswords immediately begin cutting down crops and stealing away items from the home. Before long, you're back out on the roads, your stocks now almost full. A few brothers are taking red rags to their wet blades.
units.zh: 你转过身，向{#1}弟兄甲{/#1}递了个眼色。他点头会意，搭箭上弦。女人还没来得及尖叫，他便松开弓弦。门廊上的老人中箭向后跌进屋里，一群孩子尖叫着跟了进去。其余弟兄四散开来，拔剑冲向田地。几个农工试图反抗，却被你们这支装备精良的队伍迅速杀倒。{#2}弟兄乙{/#2}冲进农舍，你听见里面传来好几声哭喊，随后一声接一声地消失，直至归于寂静。你把女人交给几个弟兄，只吩咐他们在离开前确保她已经死了。另外几个佣兵立刻动手收割庄稼，把屋里的东西搬走。没过多久，你们重新踏上道路，补给几乎装满。几个弟兄正用已经染红的破布，擦拭仍湿漉漉的刀刃。

units.source: While the company takes a short rest, you sit down to examine the wound where an arrow punctured your side not long ago. It's been healing slowly and still aches if you move too quickly, but things are getting better. {#1}Bro{/#1} joins you, seizing this opportunity to talk to his captain.
units.zh: 战团短暂歇息时，你坐下来，查看不久前侧腹中箭留下的伤口。它愈合得缓慢，动作一快仍会隐隐作痛，不过正在好转。{#1}一名弟兄{/#1}走来坐下，趁机和你这位团长谈了起来。

units.source: "So the way I see it, nobody knows about the {#1}Companyname{/#1} yet. We don't want to hunt rag-tag bands of brigands through the woods forever, but we'll have to make a name for ourselves first as reliable swords-for-hire that can get things done before the noble houses take notice. They'll want to use the company for far better paying tasks, I'm sure."
units.zh: "依我看，现在还没人听说过{#1}〈战团名〉{/#1}。我们总不能一辈子钻林子，追着那些乌合之众的强盗跑。但要让贵族家族注意到我们，就得先闯出名声，让人知道咱们靠得住，能把事情办成。到时候，他们肯定会拿报酬高得多的活儿来找我们。"

units.source: After the battle is over, you find {#1}Rookie{/#1} on his knees, his body swaying back and forth as he nurses a wound. You hear muffled cries in between all-too-loud moans. Approaching, you ask the man if he is alright. He shakes his head and explains that this was his first taste of real, vicious combat. It was not what he expected and isn't sure if he can continue.
units.zh: 战斗结束，你发现{#1}新兵{/#1}跪在地上，捂着伤口，身子前后摇晃。响亮的呻吟之间，夹着压抑的哭声。你走近，问他还好吗。他摇头解释，这是自己第一次尝到真正残酷的战斗，和想象中完全不同。他不知道还能不能撑下去。

units.source: You snap awake to a bright green hue and slap it out of your face. {#1}Hauntedbrother{/#1} falls to the ground and beside him the Grand Diviner's flail clangs. The sellsword shakes his head and his eyes widen as he looks around, confused.
units.zh: 你猛然惊醒，眼前一片亮绿，抬手便将它拍开。{#1}受惊扰的弟兄{/#1}跌倒在地，大先知的连枷也在他身旁哐当落下。佣兵晃着脑袋，茫然地睁大眼睛，四下张望。
